data.title: 'Popular dissatisfaction' across Europe: 'Promises of more economic growth haven't come true'
data.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Steven Erlanger, Chief Diplomatic Correspondent in Europe for The New York Times, based in Berlin. Europe's political centre is confronting a crisis that extends far beyond electoral volatility. From France and Germany to Italy and Spain, mounting economic frustration, generational inequality and declining confidence in established political leadership are reshaping the continent's democratic landscape. "The promises of more economic growth haven't come true," explains Erlanger, describing a continent marked by "a kind of general disgust" and "a sense of drift."

data.description: Youth-driven protests have been popping up all over Europe: in Belgium, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Albania, Serbia and Greece. data.title: In run-up to mass protests and riots, pro-Russian accounts amplified French anger, NGO finds
data.description: Research carried out by the Alliance4Europe NGO suggests that pro-Russian networks manipulated information online in an effort to exacerbate anger in France ahead of last weekend's massive protests and subsequent unrest. data.title: Trump exploits France riots to push false immigration claims ahead of midterms
data.description: Donald Trump and his inner circle are using unrest in France to push unsubstantiated claims blaming the riots on immigration, even showing French protest footage at midterm rallies. Trump’s focus comes as Republicans face mounting pressure ahead of the midterms and his approval rating hits a reported record low.

data.title: 'Neither the Sudanese military, nor the RSF take any acknowledgement of human life in this war'
data.description: The death toll from a drone strike Monday on a market in an area disputed between Sudan and South Sudan has risen to 153 and is likely even higher, a local official told AFP on Wednesday. Authorities in Abyei district said the strike on the Amiet market involved the use of multiple munitions and was carried out by the Sudanese army. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Jan Pospisil, Sudan Affairs Analyst at the Peace and Conflict Resolution Evidence Platform. He says that for a long time the Sudanese army has tried "to portray a picture internationally that they are humane, whereas RSF is committing atrocities. Here we see very clearly that there is not much difference between these two".

data.title: Everyone hates Oxford Street. Will pedestrianisation save it?
data.description: In a few days the busiest shopping street in Europe will be closed to traffic. The hope is that an unloved and polluted thoroughfare will turn into somewhere that people actually want to spend time In February, the mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, announced that Britain’s best-known thoroughfare, Oxford Street, would be pedestrianised. To the surprise of every Londoner that I have spoken to in the past few months, it is actually happening. On Monday 26 October, the busiest shopping street in Europe – or, precisely, half of its 1.2-mile stretch – will be closed to traffic, putting an end to several decades of bitter arguments, obstructions and delays. Cars, lorries, vans, taxis, buses, bicycles, ebikes, scooters will be banned. Nothing but pedestrians (and emergency vehicles) will be allowed in. This change will mark the most remarkable transformation to the streetscape of central London since at least 2003, when Trafalgar Square was turned from a glorified roundabout into one of London’s most recognisable public spaces. It will also form the most visible part of the mayor’s legacy, whether or not Khan runs for a fourth term in 2028. Three years ago, Khan published a memoir and manifesto, Breathe , attributing his asthma to growing up inhaling London’s polluted air. For the mayor, pedestrianising Oxford Street is the culmination of a mission to create a greener city that is oriented around public health, walking and cycling. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I wanted to create the female version of a man’s suit’: how Roland Mouret’s Galaxy dress took over the world
data.description: One the most famous dresses of this century, it was worn by royalty and A-list celebrities in the noughties. Its latest fans are Maga women. Here, the designer, and former mentor to Victoria Beckham, reveals the story behind it The story of one of the most photographed and ripped-off dresses of the last 50 years came together with a simple zip. It was 1998; the designer Roland Mouret had shown his first collection at London fashion week and was looking for a way to produce good clothes at speed. He connected with a small British atelier and it was there that some old-school industry wisdom would alter his course: he learned that a longer seam doesn’t actually cost any more than a shorter one. Despite his brilliantly instinctive approach to design, it was like cracking a code – and steered him towards the dress that would make his name. “My brain was buzzing!” he says. “I hadn’t thought about it before – if you extend a top by 50cm, it becomes a whole outfit. You just need accessories. Focusing on dresses gives you a signature piece at the right price.” Continue reading...

data.title: 18 again: I returned to my life in 1983 – to reckless adventures, in a world soaked in alcohol
data.description: Sundays were deadly, the generation gap between parents and their kids was enormous, and a pint cost 50p. The frisson of casual violence was everywhere. When I left school and set off to travel, I had no sense at all of where I was going or what I would find I am wandering down a steep and unfamiliar street in Saint Peter Port, Guernsey, a force seven gale blowing in my face, when I look up to cross the road and see a back garden running up the hillside opposite. It ends in a granite rock face about 30ft high, and in that moment, I have a vivid flashback to being sat on top of it, watching a group of people in the garden below. I can’t conjure their faces, but the memory is all too real: the sun on my face, a woman calling up: “Don’t break your neck!” I can tell she’s not worried and neither am I. Nobody is. It’s a party and we’re young and we’re drunk and we’re carefree, without a worry in the world. Or at least, that’s how I remember it. I continue down the street, spooked by the power of the recollection, how it has ambushed me. I stand outside the house. I could swear I’ve never seen it before. Did I come to the party over the cliff? Should I knock on the door? Hi, this is going to sound weird but I was in your back garden about 42 years ago and I haven’t a clue why but I’ve just remembered it like it was yesterday … Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’d consider replacing one of my children’: Taika Waititi on robot kids, his cheese-o-meter and Klara and the Sun
data.description: The director has turned Kazuo Ishiguro’s acclaimed novel about an ailing adolescent and her glitchy robot friend into a thought-provoking film. What do the pair think this story says about tech, love and grief? In the wings of the London film festival, a group of young influencers are discussing their personal highlights. Klara and the Sun, says one, and her colleagues agree. It’s not just that the film is still so fresh in their memory, or that they have gathered today to meet its creators and stars. Klara is funny and moving; it’s their festival favourite so far. I relay this exchange to Taika Waititi, the film’s director, who is sipping bottled water in a room down the hall. His gaze widens. He almost chokes. “Thank God!” he exclaims with just a bit too much heat. Everybody has a perfect film, just as everybody has a perfect friend, and they vary because everybody is different. In the film, sick 14-year-old Josie loves her discontinued robot doll Klara, whereas most kids her age opt for brighter, shinier models. And the young influencers love Klara and the Sun – Waititi’s adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s acclaimed novel – while most older critics vehemently, violently disagree . All of which shows that there’s no accounting for taste, that people are confounding, and that our hearts and our brains are not always in sync. That keeps life interesting. It’s partly what the film is about. “The emotions that we give very simple labels to are really complex,” says Ishiguro, who is seated alongside the director. “The thing we call love, for example, is incredibly noisy and multifaceted. Nobody knows what the hell love is.” Continue reading...

data.title: Nobody Wants This review – prepare to fall in love again … with a different couple
data.description: Adam Brody and Kristen Bell’s hit romcom is still gorgeous as Noah and Joanne move in together. But if you’re thirsty for the fizz of new romance … their siblings might set hearts aflutter Just as you and your true love can’t have a second first date or another first kiss, romantic comedies can never go back. Nothing replaces the giddy spell of the movie’s opening act or the TV show’s debut season. Sure, there can be some joy and fulfilment in a fictional relationship settling down, but really we want the crackle of chemistry, the thrill of a connection that’s brand new. Nobody Wants This is now in its third season, so it has had to leave behind the days when it was powered entirely by the phenomenal screen sparkle between Adam Brody as Noah, the rabbi who can balance devotion to his faith with the mischievous instincts of a regular thirtysomething guy; and Kristen Bell as Joanne, the atheist co-host of a frank sex-and-relationships podcast who is not as cynical or shallow as people think, or as she pretends to be. data.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for chicken with citrus and oregano | A kitchen in Rome
data.description: This dish of chicken in a lipsmacking citrus and oregano sauce has been handed down through many generations of Roman restaurateurs If you look through the window of Piatto Romano between 10am and midday, there will almost certainly be two, maybe three people at the round table trimming vegetables: chicory, artichokes, poppy greens, amaranth. After midday, the crates and trimmings will have been cleared away and the table will now be home to trays of bright-green boiled vegetables and, maybe, baked salt cod. By 12.30pm, everything will have been moved into the small kitchen in time for service, which starts at 12.45pm. When I first moved to Rome in 2005, Via Bodoni 62 was home to a restaurant called Da Rafaelle, which had white plastic chairs (inside as well) and served traditional Roman food with plenty of offal. We went to Da Rafaelle a few times before it closed in 2009. But, mostly, we went to La Torricella, which is on the other side of Testaccio and serves mainly fish. The owner is Augusto D’Alfonsi and, during lunch one day, he mentioned that he was taking over via Bodoni 62, and that his daughter Francesca would run it. They’d serve traditional Roman food with plenty of offal and it would be called Piatto Romano. This was 2011. My son was born later that year and my memories are not unpleasantly foggy; of the vegetable trolley in the corner, of chicken with red peppers and of Francesca and her father negotiating strongly. I also remember Francesca’s brother, Andrea, starting to be around more, before he eventually took over in late 2013. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Wow, logging that as a microaggression!’ Sophie Duker on trolling masculinity, lesbian cruises and her stripper fantasy
data.description: The standup on the bizarre gifts she’s received from fans, the intoxicating power of being an author and manifesting her ‘fiercely intellectual slutty grandma’ How did you get into comedy? If you want anything badly enough, the best way to get it is to feign absolute indifference while pouring in 110% effort. I was telling outrageous jokes about colonialism in tiny pub rooms five nights a week alongside a rotating lineup of lunatics and sexual deviants, all the while gaslighting myself into believing it was a casual hobby and I could stop any time. What’s been one of your all-time favourite gigs? I loved performing on a lesbian cruise, despite the debilitating impostor syndrome (I’m an omnivore). I got a record number of fist-bumps from appreciative butches and met so many incredible older sapphics. One was a black witch from California who communed with my ancestors directly after the show – you don’t get that kind of service on Live at the Apollo. Continue reading...

data.title: The Experiment review – easily the most disturbing thing on TV
data.description: As members of the public tour a fake ‘residential home’ for disabled people riddled with Nazi ideology, you desperately hope someone will speak up. Prepare for the most excruciating viewing of your life I have never had to pause a programme halfway through before to catch my breath. That is until The Experiment – Channel 4’s highly controversial social exercise designed to find out “how susceptible the British public are” to Nazi ideology about disabled people. This is a show so disturbing, timely and surreal that within 90 seconds of viewing it alone, I am looking around for confirmation from an empty room that any of this is happening. We start with a clip of Hitler. Against a backdrop of growing anti-benefits and ableist rhetoric, presenters Mat Fraser and Sophie Morgan fear the disabled community globally are once again being framed as a financial burden. Their question is: can the British public be persuaded that disabled people should live in “money saving” segregated institutions and be given low-skilled jobs to be productive? Continue reading...

data.title: Proms, parties and gender politics: amazing photos from American dancefloors – and what they tell us about a changing nation
data.description: From George Balanchine to the Rockettes, the US magazine regularly ran lavish photo spreads dedicated to dance, with the myriad ways people moved their bodies holding up a mirror to the shifting times Life magazine launched in 1936. Its aim: to show the US the world, in pictures. At a time when television was still an experimental medium, a golden age of photojournalism brought the outside world into people’s homes. Life ran weekly until 1972, spanning a transformative time in US culture. Photographers were dispatched across the globe, covering wars, political manoeuvres, social trends, hemlines and Hollywood. And in December 1936, the magazine dedicated its cover feature to dance, with dancers from the new School of American Ballet gracing the front page. As such a vividly visual medium, dance would become a regular feature in Life’s pages across the years. When I was asked to write the text for a new book featuring a collection of dance-themed images from the Life archive, it was a kid-in-a-candy-shop situation. For a dance fan there were some absolute gems to be found: the great George Balanchine crafting his ballet The Seven Deadly Sins – and cooking dinner in his Manhattan apartment; Margot Fonteyn and Rudolf Nureyev taking New York in a piece headlined The Hottest Little Team in Show Biz; or an ageing Agnes de Mille going full-throttle in rehearsal. But the archive told a much bigger story than that. It was fascinating to see the reflection of society through the way people danced: in ballrooms, nightclubs, proms and parties. In the array of social dancers: from the waltz and tango to the lindy hop, mambo, twist and the frug, themes of the 20th century play out. You can see a story of growing individualism in the shift from structured couple dancing to going freeform on the dancefloor – gender politics, too, as it was out with “May I have this dance?” and in with the democracy of the disco. Life columnist Albert Goldman asked: “Has there ever been a decade for dance like the 60s?” as he wrote of a power shift from the stage to the dancefloor, from the professional performer to the “inventive amateur”. There’s the birth of the teenager, too, bringing an explosion of pop culture and spreading dance trends on TV shows such as American Bandstand. Continue reading...

data.title: Strongmen like Trump would destroy the planet out of pure spite – and Brazil shows we’re all in peril | George Monbiot
data.description: If Flávio Bolsonaro is elected, Brazil’s ecosystems will face collapse. The ruling class would rather burn the world than share it with the poor However grim the trajectory might seem, I’ve always believed that sense will ultimately prevail. As the great perils of dismantling the living world become increasingly obvious, even the most rapacious exploiters must come round. Nobody wants to live on a dead planet, do they? There are – or were – signs that this wasn’t just wishful thinking. Since 2015, mostly thanks to China, the area of the planet being reforested has increased , while thanks in large part to Brazil, the global rate of forest destruction has declined. The area of the Brazilian Amazon forest cleared each year is one-sixth of what it was when records began in 1988. In the past four years, as a result of Brazilian government policy, the deforestation rate has fallen by 71% . If Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is re-elected president on Sunday, the country could reach zero deforestation by 2030. The arc of the moral universe seems to have bent towards justice. data.title: In You Can See Everything, it’s Elizabeth Holmes’s partner who makes for 2026’s timeliest villain
data.description: Nathan Fielder’s conversation-igniting film on the Theranos founder finds its darkest moments in her deceptive, Charlie Kirk-loving fiance Billy Evans Secrets, lies and a shock A-list cameo: how You Can See Everything became the film of the year ‘You can’t make this stuff up’: why we remain fascinated by Elizabeth Holmes It’s likely that most audiences going into the surprise documentary smash You Can See Everything are familiar with either its nominal subject (and literal poster gal with an intense stare) Elizabeth Holmes, the tech founder serving a prison sentence for defrauding investors; or the film’s on-camera co-director Nathan Fielder. Holmes, as the movie points out, was all over the media as her company Theranos was hyped to the moon and then spectacularly imploded; she was also played by Amanda Seyfried in the well-regarded Hulu miniseries The Dropout. Fielder, meanwhile, may not have graced as many magazine covers, but is similarly familiar to prestige-TV acolytes from his comedy-reality series Nathan for You and its successor, the more reality-bending series The Rehearsal. A third figure not included in the film’s ad campaign becomes a key part of the film in the second half, and will also be familiar to many viewers. This should leave Billy Evans as the odd man out. Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’s partner (she has said they’re not legally married, though they did get engaged in 2018, have two children and seem to treat each other as spouses), is a not-particularly-famous guy whose screen time competes with the other three well-known faces in what is essentially a four-character drama. But while Evans isn’t boxed out in terms of screen time or memorability, he does remain the odd man out in the sense that in all the discussion You Can See Everything has prompted about manipulation, shifting sympathies and who can or cannot be trusted, everyone seems to agree on one crucial point: Billy Evans sucks. A third figure not included in the film’s ad campaign becomes a key part of the film in the second half, and will also be familiar to many viewers. This should leave Billy Evans as the odd man out. Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’s partner (she has said they’re not legally married, though they did get engaged in 2018, have two children and seem to treat each other as spouses), is a not-particularly-famous guy whose screen time competes with the other three well-known faces in what is essentially a four-character drama. But while Evans isn’t boxed out in terms of screen time or memorability, he does remain the odd man out in the sense that in all the discussion You Can See Everything has prompted about manipulation, shifting sympathies and who can or cannot be trusted, everyone seems to agree on one crucial point: Billy Evans sucks. data.title: Is this Prince Harry or David Brent in The Office? Either way, we’re watching a masterclass in awkwardness | Emma Brockes
data.description: The wayward prince and his wife seem to be aiming for a reboot – searching for purpose, but not self-awareness Years ago, I was in Washington DC when Prince Harry blew through on an official engagement. He was 28, with a full head of hair, a slightly louche gait and a public image that, on a tour of the Senate led by a baffled-looking John McCain , caused people to lose their minds. Senate staffers stood five deep to get a glimpse; women materialised from every corner, more glamorously dressed for the office than usual. The excitement was so great that there were actual screams from behind the security line. I remember noting the prince’s prominent ears, the high colour in his cheeks and his habit, when addressed, of bowing his head, as if humbled by what he was hearing. Aw, I thought. Bless him. data.title: I’ve booked my first proper holiday – and it’s pulled me out of winter grimness like a magic spell
data.description: Anticipating a potential spring in which I am bathed in sun on a Greek island is giving me the kind of glee that makes anything feel possible Reader, it’s important to tell you that I’ve never been to Greece in my life. Not once. But I might be going, for the very first time, in the spring. And so, for the last week or so, all my dreams have featured fresh fish cooked to flaky perfection, a swimming pool into which I shall venture no deeper than my waist (I can’t swim), and the heat of the sun that not even the climate crisis can make happen in the UK in April. I don’t come with a history of exotic foreign holidays. Travelling abroad fell under the umbrella of familial duty: “Going Home”, AKA a brief return to the place where my parents were born (and coincidentally more and more foreign to them the longer they lived in the UK) in order to keep the ties of kinship going and remind us of our roots. I should say we didn’t do idyllic UK-based holidays either. I read about caravans in Enid Blyton books and watched Vaseline-lensed ads for CenterParcs and knew neither was in my immediate future. I made peace with it. We just weren’t a “going on holiday” type of family. It didn’t bother me. I harbour no resentment, and honestly, feel largely equanimous when I consider this “gap” in my life experience. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: The Guardian view on the Republicans’ midterms struggle: Trump has circuses, but voters also want bread | Editorial
data.description: As prices keep rising, more of the president’s supporters are asking what happened to the economic good times he promised It is no great revelation that Donald Trump is enriching himself as president. He raked in $2.2bn in 2025, with his position and his personal interests frequently overlapping. Yet this week’s poll finding that 34% of Republicans (and 66% of all American voters) think that he is using his position to make himself rich merits attention . Separately, voters in a Fox News poll last week put government corruption at the top of their list of concerns – just ahead of inflation and high prices. Mr Trump pledged that people would be better off if they voted for him. Billionaires are; not the rest. He promised to lower grocery costs (they have risen) and to cut the price of gasoline to below $2 a gallon. It’s more than double that, thanks to his illegal war on Iran. Tariffs haven’t helped. Incumbents struggle when life feels unaffordable, and polling for the Guardian has shown the disenchantment of key voting groups. The gulf between his own prosperity and the lives of his base now looks less like an inspiration and more like an insult. Cash offers seem unlikely to help much. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on drilling in Jackdaw: a truly pragmatic approach would focus on Britain’s green transition | Editorial
data.description: Opening the North Sea gasfield will deliver minimal benefits for households, while sending a dismal signal before next month’s Cop summit This week a report from the UN Environment Programme concluded that holding global temperatures to a 1.5C warming limit – the centrepiece commitment of the Paris climate agreement – is no longer achievable. If the disastrous consequences of a significant overshoot are to be mitigated, it argued, governments must start delivering the short-term actions to meet long-term targets on reducing fossil fuel consumption. Disappointingly, Andy Burnham and his energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, took a different view of short-term priorities on Wednesday. Before the November Cop summit, where regaining lost momentum on climate action will be crucial, their decision to approve new drilling in the Jackdaw gasfield sent a dismal signal. The prime minister justified it as a pragmatic move “at a time when people are really struggling”. But the pragmatic arguments don’t stack up. Continue reading...

data.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
data.description: For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. data.title: Welcome to the trap: swaggering Atlanta Dream turn WNBA finals into a hometown spectacle
data.description: Atlanta’s long-suffering sports fans know better than to get carried away. But the Dream’s first WNBA finals game in 13 years showed this might finally be a team worth falling for The Atlanta Dream were exactly where they wanted to be on Wednesday night, comfortably ensconced inside their downtown arena for Game 3 of the WNBA finals against the Golden State Valkyries . Kerry Washington, Ludacris and Cam Newton led the courtside celebrity delegation. Quavo and TI headlined the halftime show, while two more hugely popular Atlanta rappers performed during other extended play stoppages – a mini-spectacle that speaks to the city’s deep bench of hip-hop talent. But it was the crowd that really made State Farm Arena a house of horrors for Golden State. They didn’t just fill the 20,000-seat venue. They donned matching sky-blue T-shirts and waved rally towels. They sang along with their favorite emcees and lived and died with every point. They were so loud in the first quarter that I couldn’t hear the referee’s whistle from my 100-level press seat. They stayed to the end – well, two minutes from the buzzer anyway (gotta beat traffic) – and, with the 97-71 win sealed and DJ Khaled’s All I Do Is Win blasting through the arena speakers, serenaded the departing Valkyries with the unofficial Atlanta battle cry: “ATL hoe!” Continue reading...

data.title: How autumnal high pressure brings on the dark doldrums
data.description: With no wind to disperse the low cloud, mist and fog and less sunlight to burn it off, anticyclonic gloom can set in In summer, a high-pressure system over the UK usually means fine weather. But in the colder months it can result in anticyclonic gloom, characterised by grey skies, mist, fog and drizzle. A settled high-pressure system brings stable conditions and impedes the usual vertical movement of air. This is a recipe for sunshine when humidity is low, but can act like a lid, trapping atmospheric moisture near the surface. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It feels quite frightening’: readers rush to snap up Sally Rooney books as stocks dwindle amid Palestine Action ban
data.description: Booksellers have reported selling out of the Irish novelist’s works after it was announced that her books would be withdrawn from sale in the UK Booksellers have reported selling out of copies of Sally Rooney’s novels, following the news that her books would be withdrawn from sale in the UK, given her support for the banned group Palestine Action. Sales shot up nearly 300% in a week, as a host of high profile writers signed letters in support of the Irish author, including Zadie Smith, Annie Ernaux, Arundhati Roy, Ali Smith and Kamila Shamsie. Bookmarked, an independent bookshop in Bristol, had three Sally Rooney novels in stock when Faber announced last week that it would stop supplying the author’s books. Within hours, customers had bought all of them. Now the shop has none, and it cannot get any more. “In retrospect, I feel like we should have put them behind a glass casing, forever on display until the law is overturned,” says the shop’s general manager Evelyn. Continue reading...

data.title: Female Life on Planet Earth by Laleh Khadivi review – a mother’s secret past in the Iranian revolution
data.description: A woman living in California discovers her mother may have been a merciless enforcer of the Islamic revolution, in an intriguing novel of inheritance and identity “It’s a little scary, isn’t it, inheritance?” That’s what Heti, the protagonist of Laleh Khadivi’s latest novel, remarks to a “soccer mom” as they watch their daughters play. “We don’t get to choose what we inherit. Or what we pass on.” Heti, who lives in Los Angeles, is Iranian-American and works for an accountancy firm. She has two daughters, Ava and Zora, and her mother has recently died. When Ava scores a goal, the soccer mom asks, “Did she get that from you?”, but Heti is less interested in the skills that parents pass to their children than the secrets they keep from them. Khadivi’s novel is about mothers and the mysteries they contain. In Female Life on Planet Earth she asks what happens when the people closest to us turn out to be strangers. How do we manage our grief and memorialise our loss when those we love have hidden awful parts of their lives? At the beginning of the book, Heti receives strict instructions from an Iranian aunt about the correct way to mark her mother’s passing. “One year after the death you throw a party,” she is told, “so that [people] can think about your mother, really remember and mourn her.” But then Heti receives a startling set of photographs from an unknown sender. In one image, a younger version of her mother stands veiled in black, a machine gun slung over her shoulder. In a second image, the weapon is extended towards a group of handcuffed women, “their miniskirts uneven on their hips, rips in their tight sweaters”, some crying before the camera, another lying prone, “face pressed into the concrete floor”. Continue reading...

data.title: Ellie & Natasia review – please give us more of this irresistibly weird comedy
data.description: The hilarious duo are back with deeply silly sketches about an evil trad-wife, Lime bike addicts and Dubai chocolate. There are only three episodes, but each one is gloriously unsettling – and packed with ridiculously good guest stars In 2022, comics and actors Ellie White and Natasia Demetriou starred in six bite-size episodes of their self-titled sketch show. Among the highlights: a woman who makes wild swimming her whole personality before realising she hates freezing water; a pair of overbearing, overopinionated mums who vlog from a sterilely clean kitchen (“you’re not a real mum unless you’re redecorating or knocking through at least six times a year”) and, of course, Internet Nails, about two decidedly useless eastern European beauty entrepreneurs who were branching out into a variety of business ideas (“please let us scratch you with our ink today, and if you change your mind we can burn the tattoo off with professional match”). It was often hilarious, and was definitely weird, with many parallels to the offbeat Channel 4 series Stath Lets Flats (which White and Demetriou starred in alongside the latter’s brother, its creator Jamie). Four long years later – reportedly due to scheduling clashes – the duo are back. Ellie & Natasia series two comprises just three episodes, although – gladly – these episodes are now half an hour long rather than a mere 15 minutes. Internet Nails, in particular, remains a crucible for unsettling comedy, with the salon having become a “premiere relax styling and elegance lounge for all makeup, hair straightening and spray tanning mother-baby needs”). The fact that both women were pregnant at the time of filming only makes it funnier, and the low-rent experience (“100% birthing penthouse with perfect lukewarm Jacuzzi”) is deeply silly and – for anyone who has gone to a slightly shonky beauty shop before – astutely observed. The judgy mums are back, too, complete with advice on how to make your wardrobe stretch from “conception to birth, birth to night, night to bed, bed to menopause, menopause to coffin, and coffin to hell …” Continue reading...

data.title: Scream review – Wes Craven meta horror remains super smart and scary 30 years on
data.description: Self-aware romp through the genre is redolent of the 90s but its ghost-masked killer is as alarming as ever The 30th anniversary re-release of the original Scream, from screenwriter Kevin Williamson and director Wes Craven, brings us to a locus classicus of the 90s: a self-aware romp through the horror genre. It features Skeet Ulrich’s high schooler Billy Loomis announcing that reality is “all one big movie – but you can’t pick your genre”, which is the meta-slasher equivalent of Jacques Derrida’s belief that there is nothing outside the text. A ghost-masked killer is murdering and terrorising the bland Californian town of Woodsboro, and we begin with his gruesome assault on Casey (Drew Barrymore); he makes chilling calls to people’s landline phones, in an era where that meant you more or less had them pinned them down to a certain location. (The existence of “cellular” phones was still an exotic novelty.) The mother of teen Sidney (Neve Campbell) had been brutally killed previously, a crime pinned on local man Cotton Weary (a cameo for Liev Schreiber) who is now in jail. But was he really guilty? Now Sidney is at risk like everyone else. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘He had this electrical charge’: the short life and long legacy of Jason Molina, master of Americana
data.description: As a documentary celebrates the late US musician, friends and collaborators describe an incomparable storyteller who brought ‘myth and magic to everyday life’ Jason Molina grew up in a trailer in the working-class city of Lorain, Ohio. The city’s skyline once flickered with blue flames and a warm orange glow emanated from clattering steel mills, but by Molina’s teenage years, Lorain was in a tailspin. “Things were really on the economic decline,” says Tommy Nickoloff, Molina’s childhood friend and director of a new documentary: You Fuckers Figure It Out: A Jason Molina Story. “Nobody had any money and we were encouraged to get out. It’s a place where the American dream was born and died. And we watched it die.” Molina did indeed get out: the singer-songwriter released almost 20 studio albums and numerous EPs, primarily under the monikers Songs: Ohia and Magnolia Electric Co, spanning lo-fi to slowcore via polished Americana and alt-country. By 2009, he estimated he had written thousands of songs. But he died in 2013, aged 39, after years of alcoholism. Continue reading...

data.title: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort review – Wii Sports lives on in this effortlessly appealing collection of games
data.description: Nintendo Switch 2; Nintendo/Nintendo Bringing a holiday vibe and a generous selection of sport-themed games, this is exactly what you want from a family video game When the first Nintendo Switch Sports brought the effortless fun of Wii Sports back into my living room in 2022, I was frankly delighted . My small children discovered the pleasure of waving a controller around in enthusiastic imitation of a tennis player, and the surprising subtlety of virtual bowling, working out how to twist the wrist just right to guarantee a strike. I did not expect this game to become a family fixture for the next several years as my kids got older and climbed up the online ranks in all six of its sports (plus the two that were added as free updates). Switch Sports is so beloved in my household that the release of Switch Sports Resort this week is the most anticipated gaming event of the year. To be fair, my children are a bit young for Grand Theft Auto. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort brings three of the six sports back – tennis, bowling, and volleyball – alongside golf and basketball. Then there are seven entirely new sports: boxing, table tennis, archery, thumb wrestling, skateboarding, jetski, and piloting a little prop plane. They are all intuitive, easy to get the hang of on the first or second attempt – some have more legs than others, in the long run – and all of them, crucially, are a little bit silly. Thumb wrestling in particular is cheerfully absurd, giving your characters gigantic thumbs on hands the size of their heads. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The audience gets to be in on it’: How narrative-led gameplay is Call of Duty’s greatest weapon
data.description: As video games chase spectacle, Modern Warfare 4 makes a case for putting character and consequence at the heart of its biggest battles • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here In these strange, subdued weeks before the much-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI, there have still been some welcome surprises. Onimusha: Way of the Sword revived a half-forgotten samurai action series with much aplomb, while Silent Hill: Townfall transported all of the franchise’s bloody, dread-filled psychological horror to … the picturesque Scottish coast. Even more shocking to games writers , though, is the fact that the forthcoming Modern Warfare 4 has one of the best Call of Duty campaign modes for at least six years – and might even be up there with the original Modern Warfare trilogy. The setting is an invasion of South Korea by its northern neighbour – a setup that could have fuelled a hundred instantly forgettable Netflix films, but has proved controversial in a video game. The authoritarian regime has a new (fictitious) ruler and a powerful experimental weapon, which it’s not afraid to use as the opening gambit in an explosive attack. You take on the role of Park Hyun Jun, a conscripted South Korean soldier who, along with his small unit of similarly inexperienced grunts, gets caught in the firestorm as cities burn and enemy paratroopers fill the skies. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’m always being real’: what on earth persuades disgraced people like Elizabeth Holmes to let the cameras in?
data.description: With You Can See Everything, Holmes joins other such high-profile subjects as Lance Armstrong, Imelda Marcos and Anthony Weiner to allow film-makers to document their lives. But do they ever come out well? In You Can See Everything, convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes invites film-makers Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim into her home in a supposed act of “radical transparency”. Holmes is filmed, along with her partner, Billy Evans, and their two young children, in the weeks before starting a prison sentence for defrauding Theranos investors. “The best way for people to see who she is,” Evans says, “is to give as much access as possible into our daily lives”. It may also be the best way to market “Theranos 2.0”, which the couple are working on during filming. But the documentary questions whether Holmes is presenting her authentic self or a manufactured persona. Fielder speaks for the audience when he asks Holmes in a tense exchange whether she’s “being real” with him. “I’m always being real,” she says. That question of authenticity is at the heart of documentary film-making. You Can See Everything is as much about the ambiguous relationship between film-maker and subject as it is about Holmes herself. There is often a power struggle over narrative control in documentaries, with both sides of the dynamic wanting different outcomes from the final film. Watching You Can See Everything inevitably prompts the question: why would Holmes, days before she heads to jail, invite the scrutiny of a film crew? Continue reading...

data.title: What is Black journalism for?
data.description: In honour of Claudia Jones’ memory, I reflect on how diasporic reporting provides community and avoids being defined by the western white experience Don’t get The Long Wave delivered to your inbox? Sign up here This week, I had the great honour of delivering the Claudia Jones memorial lecture, hosted by the UK National Union of Journalists. It is partly inspired by the Long Wave and the extraordinary response it continues to receive from readers. As the newsletter turns two, I reflect, in the abridged version of the lecture below, on the importance of making space in an embattled political climate. It feels like a particularly difficult time to say anything with much certainty. We stand today in the shadow of the Black Lives Matter Movement – as well as the wreckage brought about by neoliberalism, the rise of the far right, and ongoing culture wars. In the last decade, several moments have swelled with possibility and then melted away – not quite into nothing, but certainly, less than we would like. Where do we go from here? Continue reading...

data.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: don’t want to get your Big Winter Coat out just yet? Try ‘onion dressing’
data.description: It’s time to learn the art of layering – and we’re talking a crew neck with a ballet wrap and blazer, not full-on outdoor explorer Is layering an art? Probably not in the traditional sense. We are not talking the Bayeux tapestry here. No one is going to queue round the block to admire the subtle interplay between your Uniqlo Heattech and your cashmere crewneck. Still, I think it’s nice to romanticise this stuff. The deeply unpoetic truth is that it is going to get cold and wearing one item of clothing at a time simply isn’t going to cut it. So let’s pretend that the sliver of white T-shirt beneath a jumper, the shirt collar poking out above a cardigan, or the ballet wrap over a snug top are not acts of basic thermal self-preservation, but composition. A creative statement about proportion, texture, colour and self-expression. If you have to wear half your wardrobe at once, you may as well make a masterpiece out of it. The avant-garde layering term to drop in order to sound like a connoisseur this season is onion dressing. Not the most romantic name, but a clear visual for the most refined form of layering, which is fine layers rather than hefty ones. And instead of the top layer covering all beneath it, each piece should be visible. As if we were slicing through the onion and looking at a cross-section if you will excuse me labouring the allium thing. This is layering with finesse rather than brute force. Hems and collars and cuffs give an outfit depth and texture without adding too much bulk. You want to look intriguing and multi-dimensional, not like Joey in Friends wearing all of Chandler’s clothes . Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Don’t sweat the small stuff’: hospice workers share 12 lessons about life and death
data.description: Hospice and end-of-life workers discuss what they’ve learned from their work and patients in their last moments “Hospice” can be a loaded term. Some see it as synonymous with death and “giving up”, as Courtney, a full-time hospice nurse practitioner in Missouri, puts it. But Courtney, who asked that her last name be withheld for privacy reasons, doesn’t see it that way. “Hospice is giving someone a gift,” she says of her patients, who have typically received a terminal diagnosis with a timeline of six months or less. “It is giving them the gift of being able to stay at home and eat or not eat whatever they want. It is the gift of comfort.” Continue reading...

data.title: Why has a crumbling bottle plant been rebuilt in Paris? The stunning show suggesting the future is Ghana-shaped
data.description: Fondation Cartier, Paris Ibrahim Mahama put an entire factory in this exhibition exploring Ghana before and after it was ripped to shreds by colonialism. And it’s just one dazzling installation in a show full of hope Ibrahim Mahama has dug through the ruins of post-colonial Ghana, sorted through the ashes of its ancient history, picked through the industrial detritus, the corporate waste, the piles of rubbish, and found something pretty unique: hope. Sit on one of the Asante stools in his circular Parliament of Ghosts and you can almost feel a new future being worked out right in front of you. It’s the first installation in this huge exhibition at the Fondation Cartier in Paris, and it sums Mahama up pretty neatly. He’s looking at the collapse of the Ghanaian government in 1966, the way the hope of the post-colonial project was crushed in a military coup, and he’s looking at ancient Ghanaian history, at the empires that fell centuries ago and the way colonialism tore them to shreds. But he’s not lamenting any of them. He’s not mourning. Instead, he’s reclaiming them, asking how things can be rebuilt, how we can move forwards by learning from the past. Continue reading...

With this in mind, we want to hear from people whose love life has been renewed after the age of 60. How does love in your sixties and beyond differ from romance in your twenties or thirties? data.title: 17-year-old US soldier killed in Korean War identified after 75 years; remained buried as ‘Unknown X-1642’, to be laid to rest in Maryland
data.description: Pvt. Joseph E. Boyd, who went missing in action at just 17 during the Korean War, has finally been identified decades later. His remains, previously known as Unknown X-1642, have been matched to his identity through advanced forensic techniques, including DNA testing. A dignified burial ceremony is set for October 21, 2026, in Owings Mills, Maryland, underscoring the ongoing commitment to honor missing service members from historical conflicts.

data.title: China's Bohai Bay oyster reefs show recovery, with 286 oysters per square metre
data.description: A study of oyster reef restoration in China's Bohai Bay has found encouraging signs of marine habitat recovery between 2022 and 2026. By March 2026, artificial reefs supported an average of 286 oysters per square metre, while suspended particles in the water had declined by approximately 62%. Published in Frontiers in Marine Science, the study also recorded an increase in seabed animals. However, researchers said further monitoring was needed to establish the project's long-term effectiveness.

data.title: Por que dançar faz tão bem?
data.description: A geração que ajudou a popularizar o TikTok com coreografias virais é a mesma que tem deixado as pistas mais tímidas. Basta uma rápida pesquisa nas redes sociais para encontrar centenas de vídeos sugerindo, às vezes de forma irônica, que sair para dançar já não é uma prioridade de boa parte dos jovens da Geração Z . Em tempos marcados por uma epidemia de solidão, o declínio desse tipo de lazer reduz as oportunidades de aliviar a tensão e de conexão com outras pessoas sem a mediação de uma tela. A seguir, apontamos o que está por trás desse comportamento e por que dançar faz tão bem para a saúde física e mental. Leia mais (10/22/2026 - 04h00)

data.title: Aos 67 anos, ela e seu piano rodam a América num motorhome
data.description: Quando Solange Mendes Souza era adolescente, sonhava em sair pelo mundo ao lado do irmão. O plano era frequente na época, os animados anos 1970: entrar na faculdade, trancar matrícula e sair por aí mochilando antes de aderir à chamada vida adulta. Mas um acidente que matou seu pai e o irmão suspendeu a programação, trocada pelo primeiro de seus quatro casamentos, o curso de direito, e a carreira bem-sucedida no Ministério Público Federal. Só aos 64 anos, aposentada, retomou o antigo sonho. Nascia assim o projeto do Piano Nômade. Leia mais (10/21/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: Brasil sempre existiu como utopia, mesmo antes de existir como nação
data.description: No grego, "u-topos" seria simplesmente um "não lugar". Foi nesse sentido que Thomas Morus usou o título "Utopia" em 1516, quando escreveu em latim um livro que tratava de uma sociedade idílica, que (ainda) não existia. E foi a partir daí que o uso moderno da palavra foi passando a se referir também a uma quimera: mera fantasia. Leia mais (10/21/2026 - 19h26)

data.title: Späckad spionskandal skakar Tyskland
data.description: I Tyskland pågår vad som kallas för århundradets spionskandal. Det som börjar med en uppmärksammad vårdnadstvist – en förmögen arvtagerska misstänks ha kidnappat sina egna barn – slutar hemma hos en tidigare chef för landets underrättelsetjänst. Och i hans hus hittar polisen hemligstämplade dokument, som den pensionerade chefen verkligen inte borde ha. Han är nu misstänkt för spioneri och landsförräderi – och Tyskland är i chock. Har den tidigare spionchefen sålt statshemligheter till främmande makt?

data.title: DN Debatt. ”I svensk välfärd är du och jag ofta bara en kostnad att begränsa”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Skattepengar ska ju användas ansvarsfullt, även inom skola, vård och omsorg. Men svensk välfärd har kantrat: när människa ställs mot budget tippar vågskålen ofta över till mammons sida. Till vilket moraliskt pris? Att hålla budget kan inte vara det enda måttet på gott ledarskap, skriver företagsekonomen Louise Bringselius.

data.title: Nicole Sabouné: ”I Libanon kände jag mig mer hemma än någonsin”
data.description: En resa till pappans hemland Libanon fick Nicole Sabouné att skriva sitt mest personliga album. Med ”ANA أنا” vill hon bottna i sitt ursprung, fylla ut sin andra halva och förstå varför hon är den hon är. – Vissa får reda på mycket om sitt kulturella arv från sina föräldrar. Det har inte jag. Den här skivan är ett sätt att utforska det, säger Nicole Sabouné.

data.title: Macron varnar för utländsk påverkan och kritiserar Trump för ”dumma” uttalanden
data.description: PARIS. Någon direkt utländsk påverkan har inte upptäckts i förra helgens upplopp i Frankrike, enligt president Emmanuel Macron. data.title: Äventyraren snart i mål efter 28 år: ”Jag har gjort mitt”
data.description: Engelsmannen Karl Bushby tog sig genom det ökända Darién-gapet och över ett isigt Berings sund till fots. Ändå säger den 57-årige äventyraren att det svåraste av allt har varit kärleken. Efter att i oktober ha simmat i land på brittisk mark återstår nu den sista sträckan till mamman i Hull, slutet på en 50 000 kilometer lång vandring.

data.title: Veel bomen op een klein stukje grond: Tiny Forests brengen de natuur naar de stad. ‘De afstand tot het echte bos is voor veel kinderen veel te groot’
data.description: Dik tien jaar geleden werd in Zaanstad het eerste Tiny Forest in Nederland aangeplant, een minibosje van inheemse soorten, midden in de stad. Inmiddels zijn er verspreid over het land meer dan 350 van zulke bosjes. Met een risico: „Het hangt vaak af van het enthousiasme van één persoon. Als die vertrekt, versloft het.”

data.description: Het SCP schreef onlangs dat mensen met bestaansonzekerheid het gevoel hebben ‘er niet bij te horen’ en ‘een vangnet’ missen. In de Rotterdamse wijk Delfshaven gaan buurtverbinders langs portiekflats. data.title: Czy w 2029 roku Polsce grozi samorządowe tsunami? „Jeśli tak to system jest chory”
data.description: Samo ograniczenie kadencji wójtów, burmistrzów i prezydentów nie rozwiąże problemów w systemie samorządowym. Jednak ponieważ żadna licząca się siła nie chce zreformować tego systemu, dwukadencyjność doraźnie mogłaby pomóc – uważa dr Cezary Trutkowski, prezes Fundacji Rozwoju Demokracji Lokalnej.

data.title: Władimir Putin zgodził się na wznowienie rozmów z Ukrainą, po czym zaatakował Kijów
data.description: W nocy z 21 na 22 października Kijów był celem ataku powietrznego przy użyciu pocisków balistycznych - informują władze ukraińskiej stolicy. Do ataku doszło po tym, jak - po rozmowach ze specjalnym wysłannikiem prezydenta USA Stevem Witkoffem - Władimir Putin zgodził się na powrót do rozmów trójstronnych z udziałem USA, Rosji i Ukrainy. Tej samej nocy nad obwodem moskiewskim miało pojawić się 630 ukraińskich dronów.

data.title: Malování na obličej, koncert i zdobení dýní. Majaland oslaví Halloween ve velkém
data.description: Zábavní park Majaland se na Halloween připravil týdnem plným zábavy. Program dětem nabídne prolézačky, atrakce, tvořivé dílny, malování na obličej a chybět nebude ani oblíbený koncert zpěvačky Báry Landrové. V největším krytém zábavním parku v Česku mohou návštěvníci oslavit svátek hrůzy mezi 26. říjnem a 1. listopadem.

data.title: Poslanci projednají rozpočet, opozice chce omluvu Ševčíka šéfce klubu STAN
data.description: Poslanci budou pokračovat v prvním čtení návrhu státního rozpočtu na příští rok se schodkem 386 miliard korun, což nedokončili ve středu před půlnocí. Ráno se Sněmovna věnovala odpovědím členů vlády na písemné interpelace. Opoziční politici se snažili přimět poslance SPD Miroslava Ševčíka, který v noci pokřikoval na šéfku poslanců STAN Michaelu Šebelovou, ať si vezme menopauzu.

data.title:
Ševčík se ve Sněmovně utrhl na Šebelovou.
Vezměte si menopauzu, vzkázal jí
data.description: STAN i další opoziční poslanci zuří. Reagují na incident ze včerejšího pozdního jednání Sněmovny. Šéf Starostů Vít Rakušan tvrdí, že poslanec Miroslav Ševčík (SPD) častoval slovy o menopauze svoji kolegyni Michaelu Šebelovou, jež žádala o pauzu v jednání Sněmovny. Výměna názorů, do níž se podle Rakušana zapojil za použití sprostých slov i šéf Sněmovny Tomio Okamura, vyvrcholila v hádku. Okamura se podle svých slov snažil naopak situaci zklidnit.

data.title: Evropa se musí změnit, jinak bude irelevantní, varoval Pavel pro německý list
data.description: Američané a Rusové neberou Evropu vážně, protože vidí, jak je rozdělená a jak zdlouhavě přijímá svá rozhodnutí. Evropa se proto musí změnit, aby se nestala irelevantní. V rozhovoru s nejčtenějším německým deníkem, bulvárním listem Bild, to řekl prezident Petr Pavel, který je nyní na dvoudenní návštěvě Německa. Ruským cílem je nyní mimo jiné vyvolat novou uprchlickou vlnu z Ukrajiny do Evropy, míní.

data.title: Trumpova muže sráží skandály. Demokraté mohou mít po 40 letech senátora za Texas
data.description: Jeden z nejnapínavějších soubojů ve volbách do amerického Kongresu se odehraje v Texasu, kde by demokraté mohli získat křeslo v Senátu po bezmála 40 letech. Texaský zákonodárce James Talarico, který je považován za vycházející hvězdu Demokratické strany, se utká s republikánem Kenem Paxtonem, texaským generálním prokurátorem provázeným řadou skandálů. A právě v Texasu by navíc republikánští kandidáti mohli pocítit slábnoucí podporu hispánských voličů, kteří v předloňských prezidentských volbách výrazně pomohli Donaldu Trumpovi k návratu do Bílého domu.

data.title: Řidič ujížděl v protisměru bez světel. Zastavily ho až výstřely a speciální manévr
data.description: Zběsilou noční honičku řešila hlídka z cizinecké policie v Praze 2. Řidič se snažil policisty setřást, vjížděl do protisměru a ohrožoval ostatní vozy. V jednu chvíli dokonce vypnul světla na autě a jel potmě. Policie musela využít speciálního PIT manévru, aby muže zastavila.

data.title: Opakované útoky na Kyjev zranily 24 lidí, rakety zničily domy, metro i čerpací stanici
data.description: Ruské raketové útoky v noci na čtvrtek v Kyjevě zabily jednoho člověka, dalších 24 zranily, oznámila Státní služba pro mimořádné situace (DSNS). Podle starosty Vitalije Klička je kromě jiného poničena část infrastruktury metra na Jižním mostě přes Dněpr. Ukrajina podnikla dronový nálet na Moskvu a její okolí.

data.title: Miliardové škody, dva obvinění. Policie šetří investice do aquaponických farem
data.description: Policie obvinila dva lidi z investičního podvodu s dvoumiliardovou škodou. Případ se týká zejména investic do projektů aquaponických farem, tedy zařízení kombinujících chov ryb a pěstování rostlin. Poškozených klientů je zhruba 5000, stíhané dvojici hrozí až desetileté vězení. Dnes o tom informoval mluvčí Národní centrály proti organizovanému zločinu Jaroslav Ibehej.

data.title: Pobočky už nerušit. Nový ředitel České pošty ukázal, jak podnik promění
data.description: Česká pošta představila plán transformace, která ji má proměnit v konkurenceschopný podnik. Konkrétní kroky představil na tiskové konferenci generální ředitel Richard Hodul. Transformace se podle něj zaměří na spolehlivější doručování, dostupnější pobočky a širší nabídku služeb. Při jedné návštěvě mají zákazníci vyřídit více záležitostí, od zásilek přes finanční služby až po pomoc při komunikaci se státem.

data.title: Po roce a půl v zajetí konečně na svobodě. Rakušanku a Švýcarku drželi v Nigeru
data.description: Rakušanka a Švýcarka, které byly více než rok v zajetí v Nigeru, dorazily do východolibyjského města Benghází. Rakouská občanka, již rakouské úřady identifikovaly jako Evu Gretzmacherovou a které je přes 70 let, byla unesena v lednu 2025 v pouštním městě Agadez ve středním Nigeru. Která skupina ji zadržovala nebo jaké požadavky případně vznesla, není jasné.

data.title: Nový irský zemědělský návrh. Dobrovolný strop dotací na sedmi milionech korun
data.description: Za rok a několik měsíců by měla začít platit nová evropská zemědělská politika. Zatím však není jasné prakticky nic. Podle nového návrhu irského předsednictví EU by mohlo být tzv. zastropování evropských přímých dotací benevolentnější než předchozí plán, který počítal s maximální výší dotací 100 tisíc eur (tedy 2,4 milionu korun) na farmu a postupným snižováním plateb od 20 tisíc eur.

data.title: Saido Berahino : La révérence d’un enfant de Bujumbura
data.description:
Il y a des lettres qui ne se lisent pas. Elles se ressentent. Celle que Saido Berahino a déposée ce mardi 20 septembre 2026 sur Instagram appartient à cette race rare. 
 L'enfant prodige de Bujumbura, devenu flamme des Hawthorns, vient de raccrocher les crampons. Non pas dans le fracas, mais dans une pudeur immense, une gratitude presque sacrée.

data.title: Le soir où le Parc devint opéra : Paris terrasse Barcelone (4-2)
data.description:
Il y a des soirs où le football cesse d'être un sport. Il devient drame, il devient lyre, il devient serment. Ce mardi 20 octobre, sous les cieux allumés du Parc des Princes, le Paris Saint-Germain a offert au FC Barcelone sa première désillusion de la saison, au terme d'une symphonie en quatre actes : 4-2. 
 Une victoire d'une beauté cruelle, tant elle fut conquise dans la douleur.

data.title: L’épidémie d’Ebola signalée au Nigeria, le Cameroun affute son système de riposte
data.description: © DR Le gouvernement camerounais active la stratégie de crise sanitaire pour prévenir une éventuelle importation de la maladie sur le territoire national. Le Nigeria, pays voisin du Cameroun, a confirmé le 20 octobre dernier son premier cas de la maladie à virus Ebola, souche bundibugyo. Il s’agit d’une diplomate venue de l’Ouganda et qui a été prise en charge dans un hôpital privé à Abuja. Ce cas a permis d’identifier 44 cas contacts. Et les autorités ont renforcé la surveillance sanitaire ainsi que des contrôles aux frontières. Au Cameroun voisin, l’heure est à l’activation des mesures d’urgence pour prévenir l’importation de la maladie. Le 2 octobre dernier, le Premier ministre chef du gouvernement a réuni les autorités sanitaires en vue de l’évaluation de la situation liée à cette épidémie. Au cours de la réunion qu’il a présidée dans son cabinet à Yaoundé, Joseph Dion Ngute a tenu à savoir ce que le département ministériel chargé de la santé a déjà fait au moment où l’épidémie est aux portes du Cameroun, juste au Nigeria. D’après le ministre de la Santé publique au sortir de cette rencontre, le Cameroun n’enregistre à date, aucun cas suspect. Il est question d’assurer la préparation aux événements de santé publique avant leur arrivée. Parce que lorsque les mesures suivent la crise, celle-ci coûte plus cher, a-t-il confié aux médias. Après cette réunion à l’immeuble Etoile à Yaoundé, le ministre de la Santé publique préside une autre rencontre de crise ce jeudi au centre de coordination des opérations d’urgence de santé publique à Yaoundé. La réunion permettra de faire une évaluation du niveau de préparation du pays face à une éventuelle entrée du virus Ebola. Cette évaluation aboutira sur des mesures à prendre pour mettre à niveau la stratégie de riposte. Au sortir de cette réunion, le ministre Malachie Manaouda entend multiplier des rencontres à d’autres niveaux, en l’occurrence au niveau des entrées du pays. Présente au Nigeria, le virus Ebola fait déjà des ravages dans d’autres pays d’Afrique. Le plus grand foyer se trouve en République Démocratique du Congo où les autorités déclarent 9 952 cas confirmés dont 4 602 décès au 19 octobre 2026. Le virus est aussi présent en Ouganda, au Kenya. Comme Cameroun, le Bénin aussi multiplie des réunions pour préparer la riposte. Cet article L’épidémie d’Ebola signalée au Nigeria, le Cameroun affute son système de riposte est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : scène de chaos maîtrisée au lycée technique de Nsam après l’annonce du décès d’un élève
data.description: © DR Des élèves en colère ont pris pour cible les infrastructures du lycée technique bilingue de Nsam ce mercredi en représailles contre l’administration. L’intervention de l’autorité administrative et des Forces de maintien de l'ordre a permis de ramener la situation au calme. Une scène de manifestation menée par des élèves du Lycée technique bilingue de Nsam a laissé des séquelles sur des infrastructures de l’établissement scolaire. Des élèves en colère après avoir appris la rumeur selon laquelle leur camarade renvoyé peu avant pour coiffure non conforme était décédé suite à un accident de la circulation, ont pris d’assaut les bâtiments, détruisant ces infrastructures. Le restaurant, les bureaux administratifs, les véhicules, les salles informatiques et les tableaux numériques ont subi des attaques. Pourtant, selon un communiqué attribué à la cellule de communication du ministre des Enseignements secondaires, l’élève renvoyé ce matin n’était pas concerné par l’accident survenu. Ce mercredi matin, trois élèves de ce lycée se rendaient à l’école à bord d’une même moto conduite par l’un d’eux. Ils ont eu un accident de la circulation en chemin. L’un d’eux, le conducteur, est décédé sur le champ. Le deuxième est plongé dans le coma. Le troisième ne présentait pas de danger immédiat. Toujours selon cette communication, peu avant la nouvelle de cet accident, les surveillants du lycée ont chassé un autre élève pour coiffure non conforme. Ayant appris le décès, certains de ses camarades au lycée ont cru à tort qu’il était la victime de l’accident. D’où les attaques contre les infrastructures. Avant la fin de la journée, la situation est tout de même sous contrôle. L’intervention du sous-préfet de l’arrondissement de Yaoundé III, des Forces de maintien de l’ordre et des responsables des services déconcentrés compétents du ministère des Enseignements secondaires ont effectué une descente dans l’établissement et ont maitrisé la situation. Cet article Cameroun : scène de chaos maîtrisée au lycée technique de Nsam après l’annonce du décès d’un élève est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Numérique : la Banque Mondiale lance sa première stratégie pour l’Afrique et les pays en développement
data.description: © DR Depuis Séoul, le Groupe de la Banque mondiale a dévoilé le 20 octobre 2026 sa première stratégie numérique axée sur quatre priorités : connectivité, appareils abordables, compétences et IA. Un plan crucial pour l'Afrique où seuls 23% des habitants des pays à faible revenu utilisent internet. L'Afrique au cœur de la bataille numérique. Le Groupe de la Banque mondiale a lancé ce 20 octobre 2026 à Séoul sa première stratégie pour le numérique, qui vise à aider les pays en développement à étendre l'accès à un coût abordable, à améliorer les services et à créer des emplois. "Les technologies numériques peuvent aider les pays à créer des emplois et à optimiser des ressources limitées", souligne Ajay Banga, président du Groupe. Ce lancement intervient dans un contexte critique : au cours des 10 à 15 prochaines années, 1,2 milliard de jeunes atteindront l'âge de travailler dans les pays en développement, pour seulement 420 millions d'emplois prévus. Pour l'Afrique, l'enjeu est vital. En 2025, plus de 2 milliards de personnes dans le monde n'étaient pas connectées. Seules 23% des personnes vivant dans des pays à faible revenu utilisaient internet, contre 94% dans les pays à revenu élevé. Et même en zone couverte, beaucoup ne peuvent s'offrir un smartphone ou un forfait data. La stratégie s'articule autour de quatre axes. D'abord, développer une connectivité fiable, des câbles sous-marins aux foyers, écoles et centres de santé, en s'appuyant sur les infrastructures partagées et les garanties pour attirer le privé. Ensuite, rendre appareils et données plus abordables en soutenant la baisse des prix des smartphones d'entrée de gamme via des partenariats avec fabricants, opérateurs et établissements financiers. Troisième pilier : développer les services et compétences numériques, avec des systèmes fiables d'identification, de paiement dématérialisé et de formation orientée vers l'emploi. Enfin, renforcer la préparation à l'IA. L'accent est mis sur les "petites IA", des outils adaptés aux conditions locales : détecter des maladies pour les agriculteurs, appuyer les agents de santé ou aider les entreprises à gérer leurs stocks. Les dispositifs de protection, confidentialité des données, cybersécurité et lutte contre la fraude, sont transversaux. Une stratégie qui peut soutenir la création d'emplois dans cinq secteurs clés pour l'Afrique : infrastructures et énergie, agro-industrie, santé, tourisme et industrie manufacturière. Cet article Numérique : la Banque Mondiale lance sa première stratégie pour l’Afrique et les pays en développement est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

Seules 23% des personnes vivant dans des pays à faible revenu utilisaient internet, contre 94% dans les pays à revenu élevé. Et même en zone couverte, beaucoup ne peuvent s'offrir un smartphone ou un forfait data. La stratégie s'articule autour de quatre axes. D'abord, développer une connectivité fiable, des câbles sous-marins aux foyers, écoles et centres de santé, en s'appuyant sur les infrastructures partagées et les garanties pour attirer le privé. Ensuite, rendre appareils et données plus abordables en soutenant la baisse des prix des smartphones d'entrée de gamme via des partenariats avec fabricants, opérateurs et établissements financiers. Troisième pilier : développer les services et compétences numériques, avec des systèmes fiables d'identification, de paiement dématérialisé et de formation orientée vers l'emploi. Enfin, renforcer la préparation à l'IA. L'accent est mis sur les "petites IA", des outils adaptés aux conditions locales : détecter des maladies pour les agriculteurs, appuyer les agents de santé ou aider les entreprises à gérer leurs stocks. Les dispositifs de protection, confidentialité des données, cybersécurité et lutte contre la fraude, sont transversaux. Une stratégie qui peut soutenir la création d'emplois dans cinq secteurs clés pour l'Afrique : infrastructures et énergie, agro-industrie, santé, tourisme et industrie manufacturière. Cet article Numérique : la Banque Mondiale lance sa première stratégie pour l’Afrique et les pays en développement est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: PAIDATA : le gouvernement et le FIDA lancent une mission conjointe de supervision
data.description: © DR Le ministre de l'Agriculture Gabriel Mbairobe a présidé le lundi 19 octobre 2026 à Yaoundé le lancement de la mission conjointe de supervision Gouvernement-FIDA du projet d'appui à l'intensification durable de l'agriculture et à la transition agroécologique. Accélérer avant la clôture de mars 2027. L'Administrateur du FODECC, M. Samuel Donatien Nengue, a pris part le lundi 19 octobre 2026 à la cérémonie de lancement de la mission conjointe de supervision Gouvernement-FIDA et d'appui à la mise en œuvre du PAIDATA. La cérémonie, présidée par le ministre de l'Agriculture et du Développement rural, M. Gabriel Mbairobe, s'est tenue dans la salle de conférence du MINADER à Yaoundé. La rencontre a réuni les représentants du MINEPAT, du MINFI, de la Caisse autonome d'amortissement, les responsables des directions du MINADER, ainsi qu'une importante délégation du Fonds international de développement agricole conduite par son directeur pays, M. Eric Rwabidadi. Les responsables du PAIDATA, de l'IRAD et d'autres projets bénéficiant des financements du FODECC étaient également présents. Prévue du 19 au 30 octobre 2026, cette mission a pour objectifs d'évaluer les performances du projet, d'examiner les réalisations techniques et financières, d'identifier les contraintes opérationnelles et de formuler des recommandations pour renforcer l'efficacité des interventions sur le terrain. À cette occasion, l'Administrateur du FODECC a présenté l'état d'avancement des diligences engagées pour satisfaire aux conditions de décaissement des ressources additionnelles du partenariat CAFI. Il a réaffirmé les efforts pour accélérer les procédures administratives et renforcer la justification des résultats, avec pour ambition de mobiliser les ressources disponibles avant la clôture du projet, prévue en mars 2027. Autre perspective majeure : la finance verte. M. Samuel Donatien Nengue a également évoqué les préparatifs liés à cette orientation stratégique, qui doit positionner le FODECC au cœur du financement de la transition agroécologique. Cet article PAIDATA : le gouvernement et le FIDA lancent une mission conjointe de supervision est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : la première journée mondiale de la santé environnementale célébrée à Yaoundé
data.description: © DR Célébrée pour la première fois le 19 octobre 2026 au Palais des Congrès de Yaoundé, la Journée mondiale de la santé environnementale a placé la science au cœur de la protection des communautés face à la pollution et à la dégradation des écosystèmes. Une première aux accents d'alerte. Le Cameroun a célébré pour la première fois, le 19 octobre 2026 au Palais des Congrès de Yaoundé, la Journée mondiale de la santé environnementale, sous le thème : "la santé environnementale : s'appuyer sur la science pour protéger les communautés". Habituellement célébrée le 26 septembre depuis 2011, cette journée vise à sensibiliser décideurs, professionnels et grand public au rôle déterminant de la santé environnementale dans la prévention des maladies. Au Cameroun, le lien est direct. La santé publique est impactée par la dégradation des écosystèmes, la gestion inappropriée des déchets et leur brûlage sauvage qui libère des toxines, la pollution de l'air à Douala et Yaoundé où les particules fines franchissent les seuils de sécurité, et l'insalubrité de l'eau. Les conséquences sont lourdes : maladies hydriques, affections respiratoires, prolifération des vecteurs. Les formations sanitaires reçoivent chaque jour enfants, mères et travailleurs souffrant de toux chronique, d'asthme sévère et d'infections aiguës causées par les émissions des transports et les poussières. Face à cela, le Gouvernement applique la stratégie "une seule santé". Parmi les actions concrètes : déploiement massif d'un réseau de surveillance de la qualité de l'air en temps réel via des stations fixes et mobiles, renforcement des contrôles et inspections environnementales, et soutien aux acteurs de terrain et municipalités à travers des initiatives de salubrité publique. Présidant la cérémonie, le Ministre de l'Environnement a appelé à la responsabilité de tous : collectivités, société civile, médias et secteur privé doivent respecter la législation environnementale. Aux citoyens, il a lancé un appel simple : "ne pas jeter d'ordures dans les drains, planter un arbre, préserver nos cours d'eau, l'arrêt définitif des feux de poubelles". Cet article Cameroun : la première journée mondiale de la santé environnementale célébrée à Yaoundé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Coopération Camerou-Royaume Uni : le MINPMEESA mobilise de nouveaux partenariats pour la filière bois
data.description: © DR Le ministre Achille Bassilekin III a reçu le conseiller principal forêts du Royaume-Uni, Neil Scotland. Au menu : transformation locale du bois, développement des PME forestières et valorisation durable des ressources, avec en vitrine le SMEs Wood's Park de Lomié. Yaoundé veut verdir sa diplomatie économique. Le Ministre des Petites et Moyennes Entreprises, de l'Économie Sociale et de l'Artisanat, Achille Bassilekin III, a accordé une audience à M. Neil Scotland, Conseiller principal pour les forêts au ministère britannique des Affaires étrangères, du Commonwealth et du Développement (FCDO). Il était accompagné de Mme Samantha Smith, Haut-Commissaire adjointe et Chargée d'Affaires, et de M. Euan McCarthy, Conseiller régional en climat et environnement pour l'Afrique centrale. Au cœur des échanges : le renforcement de la coopération bilatérale en faveur de la transformation locale du bois, du développement des PME forestières, de la modernisation des équipements, du transfert de technologies et de la mobilisation de financements adaptés aux entreprises camerounaises. Une priorité pour le gouvernement camerounais qui entend faire de la valorisation responsable des ressources forestières un levier de croissance, de compétitivité et de développement durable. Cette dynamique trouve une illustration concrète dans le SMEs Wood's Park de Lomié, dont la convention de partenariat entre le MINPMEESA et la Commune de Lomié a été signée le 6 octobre 2026. Ce projet vise à favoriser le développement des PME, des artisans et des organisations de l'économie sociale, tout en stimulant la création d'emplois et la production de biens à plus forte valeur ajoutée. À travers ces perspectives de coopération, le MINPMEESA entend affirmer son crédo : pour des PME plus compétitives et une transformation locale créatrice de valeur, au bénéfice des entreprises et de l'économie nationale. Cet article Coopération Camerou-Royaume Uni : le MINPMEESA mobilise de nouveaux partenariats pour la filière bois est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : le MRC remonté contre Times TV, la chaîne de télévision présente des excuses
data.description: © DR La chaîne de télévision présente ses excuses au Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun qui a exprimé son indignation face aux propos tenus par Serge Olama et Willy Mengue sur les antennes de ladite chaîne. Entre le Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun et Times TV, le climat s’oriente vers l’apaisement après le cri de colère du parti politique lancé le mardi 20 octobre. Le MRC a condamné dans un communiqué la complaisance de la chaine de télévision marquée par l’invitation de Willy Mengue ancien militant exclu du parti et l’absence de recadrage de ce dernier ainsi que de Serge Olama invité pour sa part en septembre. Ce dernier a, rappelle le parti présidé par Tiriane Balbine Noah, tenu des propos diffamatoires à l’encontre du MRC et de certains de ses responsables. Il s’agit des propos portant atteinte à la dignité de l’ancien président Maurice Kamto, de ceux traitant Olivier Bibou Nissack de « déséquilibré » et de ceux alléguant que le Pr Alain Fogue était « terroriste » et « tribaliste ». Qu’il a « lancé une cabale contre Cabral ». Le parti politique a alors exigé que Times TV et les médias cesse d’offrir des plateaux aux exclus ; que le CNC et la justice fassent la lumière sur les propos tenus sur Times TV, que « l’on cesse de confondre liberté d’expression et liberté de diffamer ». Le même jour, la télévision de Joël Kouemo a présenté ses excuses au MRC. Dans une communication, la chaîne de télévision dit prendre au sérieux les préoccupations exprimées par le parti politique. « Times TV présente ses regrets aux responsables du MRC visés par des propos outrageants et des attaques personnelles au cours de certaines de ses émissions ». La chaîne reconnait dans le même document des manquements lors de ces émissions décriées par la formation politique. Il s’agit en l’occurrence des manquements d’abord sur l’encadrement des intervenants. A ce sujet, « la confrontation des opinions, même vive, doit préserver la dignité des personnes et s’appuyer sur des arguments et des faits vérifiables », regrette la chaine. Ensuite sur la présentation de ces derniers, celle de Willy Mengue en particulier. Présenté sur l’affiche comme « homme politique MRC », il s’est réclamé du « MRC originel » au cours de l’émission. Une présentation initiale ambiguë, reconnait la chaîne. Ainsi, la chaîne de télévision s’engage à renforcer la vigilance dans la conduite des débats et réaffirme l’ouverture de ses portes aux Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun. Cet article Cameroun : le MRC remonté contre Times TV, la chaîne de télévision présente des excuses est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
