data.title: ASSIST Software Engineers Win Volkswagen Challenge for Automated Quality Inspection
data.description: ASSIST Software GmbH , the German subsidiary of Romania's ASSIST Software, has been named one of two winners of the Volkswagen Automated Inspection Challenge. Organized by Volkswagen Group Innovation and Startup Factory boOst, the competition focused on automating the final inspection of cylinder heads at Volkswagen's engine plant in Chemnitz, Germany. The recognition follows the work of an ASSIST engineering team on a manufacturing problem that demands close attention to both visible defects and inspection conditions. The assignment covered 157 drill holes and 24 surfaces across all six sides of a cylinder head, with teams required to demonstrate detection performance using real component samples. For ASSIST, the objective was to approach the task with the contextual judgment of an experienced inspector. Identifying an unusual mark is one step; determining whether it represents damage, an acceptable variation, or a misleading reflection requires a fuller assessment of the component and the available evidence. Building on the judgment of experienced inspectors "Our goal was to build a system that approaches inspection as an expert would. An experienced inspector considers the context, checks the component from the necessary angles, and knows when something needs a closer look. We wanted to account for those details, including the ones a machine might otherwise overlook." said Alexandru Boca, Robotics Expert and Head of the Mobile Department at ASSIST Software. Alexandru Boca Boca represented ASSIST at the event alongside Gabriel Tironeac, VP of Innovation; Tudor Andronic, AI Engineer; Cristina Tironeac, Project Manager; and Teodor Drobota, Business Operations Specialist. The delegation brought together expertise in robotics and innovation, project delivery, and business operations, representing the wider team behind the entry. The challenge required that expertise be applied against defined manufacturing requirements. Reflective metal can conceal a defect or create the appearance of one. Recessed holes and internal features can remain difficult to observe, even when the surrounding surface is clearly visible. Small changes in positioning can alter the images available for assessment. These conditions make inspection coverage an engineering priority. Before software can assess a feature, the system must capture enough detail to support that assessment. A feature that has not been observed adequately cannot simply be treated as acceptable. Meeting the demands of automotive production According to the organizers, hundreds of thousands of cylinder heads undergo manual inspection at the Chemnitz plant each year. The competition sought an automated solution that could meet quality requirements and allow experienced employees to focus on other tasks. The task also demanded attention to the consequences of incorrect decisions. A missed defect can allow an unsuitable component to continue through production. An unnecessary rejection creates additional checking work. A useful inspection system must therefore detect relevant faults while limiting false alarms that place further demands on factory staff. Speed matters throughout the process. Moving the component, acquiring images, and analyzing them all contribute to inspection time. More viewpoints may improve visibility, but extend the sequence; greater image detail may require additional processing. Teams had to consider these choices alongside the practical constraints of integrating a solution into a production line. Volkswagen's evaluation framework reflected those requirements, considering detection performance, processing speed, and cost-effectiveness. The challenge gave participating engineers a concrete setting in which to connect technical development with a manufacturer's expectations. Recognition after development, testing and demonstration The competition program included problem analysis, prototype development and testing before a final demonstration and jury evaluation. Volkswagen Group Innovation provided feedback at defined stages and assessed the results, while Startup Factory boOst coordinated the process and communication with participating teams. For the Suceava-based company and its German subsidiary, selection as one of two winners provides a specific automotive reference for the team's industrial inspection work. It recognizes an entry developed around a real production task, in which quality decisions depend on the interaction among imaging, software, and manufacturing requirements. As a follow-up possibility, the organizers regarded a rollout at a Volkswagen production plant, provided that it received a favorable assessment. The next stage would then involve evaluating the suggested approach further in light of the production conditions.

data.title: Romania’s justice minister hopes magistrates will accept gradual payment of EUR 1 bln in wage arrears
data.description: The Constitutional Court recently ruled in favour of magistrates seeking immediate payment of claims worth RON 5 billion (EUR 1 billion), bringing the dispute between the executive and the High Court of Cassation and Justice to a close. Marinescu said an agreement on rescheduling the payments had previously existed but was not honoured by former prime minister Ilie Bolojan, B1tv.ro reported. The claims stem from court rulings ordering the retroactive recalculation of bonuses awarded to magistrates. “The current government, which assumes a very important responsibility in managing public affairs in a difficult economic moment, marked by a sharp economic deterioration in recent months, has the mission of finding a formula for paying off these debts without unbalancing the public budget,” the justice minister said. Marinescu also responded to Ilie Bolojan’s remarks at a press conference presenting his record in office at the Victoria Palace. The former prime minister described the amounts awarded to magistrates as salary entitlements as immoral. Marinescu said he remained confident that magistrates would agree to dialogue on finding a solution.

data.title: Romania’s new government to maintain turnover tax on banks in 2027
data.description: The additional tax on oil and gas companies (ICAS) is also likely to remain in some form, given the sector’s exceptional profits, which the government considers a potential source of additional revenue, according to information obtained by Profit.ro . By contrast, the tax on special constructions, commonly known as the “pole tax”, is expected to expire as scheduled on January 1, 2027. The banking sector’s additional turnover tax is currently due to expire on December 31, 2026. Although its elimination has been discussed previously, the tax was retained and significantly increased in the summer of 2025. For 2026, it was expected to generate RON 2.7 billion in budget revenue, on top of other taxes and duties, including corporate income tax. The elimination of IMCA, which applies to companies with annual turnover exceeding EUR 50 million, is included in the government programme. Finance minister Alexandru Nazare previously said that a decision on ICAS would be made during preparations for next year’s budget. However, Profit.ro’s latest information suggests that the oil and gas sector is unlikely to escape additional taxation altogether.

data.title: Italian furniture producer Natuzzi shifts more production to Romania
data.description: The move is expected to improve margins, which have been heavily affected by declining sales volumes. “The relocation of production to Romania is expected to contribute to margin improvement,” the group’s founder and president, Pasquale Natuzzi, said, as cited by Profit.ro . Natuzzi previously estimated that the transferred production would generate an annual business volume of EUR 30–40 million, with a preliminary EBIT margin of 25% in the first year of operations. The group operates in Romania through its Italsofa factory in Baia Mare, which produces sofas and armchairs under the Natuzzi Editions brand, as well as unbranded furniture. In 2019, Natuzzi transferred production lines from China to Italy in an attempt to avoid tariffs imposed by US president Donald Trump on Chinese exports. Some of the Chinese production was also relocated to Romania.

data.title: Fitch affirms Romanian Romgaz at BBB-/negative
data.description: The negative outlook reflects the outlook on Romania's sovereign rating. Romgaz's BBB- rating benefits from a one-notch uplift from its bb+ standalone credit profile (SCP) for state support, under the rating agency’s Government-Related Entities (GRE) Rating Criteria. Among the key rating drivers is the good progress made in the Neptun Deep offshore gas project. Neptun Deep has achieved major milestones in 2026: the Neptun Alpha production platform was installed in the Black Sea in July 2026, the 160-km export pipeline to Tuzla is complete, and seven of 10 development wells have been drilled, the rating agency said. Romgaz and OMV Petrom will complete the remaining Domino field wells, install subsea infrastructure and umbilicals, finish the Tuzla metering station, and conduct testing and commissioning. First gas remains on track for 2027, with plateau production of about 8 bcm/year. Steady progress with development of the project is positive for Romgaz's credit profile. Fitch sees the Neptun Deep project as a transformational project for Romgaz. It will allow Romgaz to increase natural gas production to about 160 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day (mboe/d) from 86 mboe/d in 2025, halting a stable to declining production trend from existing mature reservoirs. The project will also secure Romania's energy independence and position the country as the EU's largest natural gas producer from domestic resources. It views execution risk as manageable, given the partner's experience in oil and gas project development. Another key rating driver is the Iernut gas-fired power plant, which approaches completion. Romgaz is making advances in the construction of the Iernut combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) power plant after considerable delay, which it expects will start production in 1Q27. Romgaz will benefit from sales of electricity on the balancing market, which it expects to increase in importance as renewable electricity generation rises with its inherent output volatility. The addition of electricity sales EBITDA from 2027 will improve the company's business diversification, although upstream activity will remain the dominant cash flow contributor. A key driver with a negative impact on Romgaz is the regulated gas price. The Romanian government implemented regulations to protect consumers in the gas supply market, in response to the Russia-Ukraine war. A majority of Romgaz's gas sales is at regulated prices, which amounted to RON 120 per megawatt hour (MWh) from April 2024 to March 2026. The capped price was reduced to RON 110/MWh from April 2026. Sales at these regulated prices are exempt from windfall taxes, and royalties are based on capped prices. Current regulation extends till end-March 2027.

data.title: Turkey’s Entek Elektrik to build 600 MWh battery storage facility near 214 MW PV park in Romania
data.description: The estimated cost of the battery investment is EUR 40 million, according to Economica.net . The project envisages a storage facility with a total power output of 300 MW and a storage capacity of 600 MWh. The first phase will provide 300 MWh of storage capacity, equivalent to 150 MW for two hours, with a further 300 MWh planned in the second phase, according to the project documents. Econergy developed the photovoltaic project before agreeing to sell it to Entek Elektrik in June 2024. The initial transaction value was EUR 32.9 million. Upon completion in 2025, Tüpraş said the amount had been revised to EUR 33.2 million, of which EUR 29.2 million had been paid by that point. In August 2026, Entek Elektrik secured EUR 71 million in financing from Banca Transilvania for the construction of the solar park, whose investment value is estimated at around EUR 100 million. Tüpraş, controlled by the Koç family, is Turkey’s largest oil refining company.

data.title: Weekend calendar: Les Films de Cannes, Bucharest Scenography Biennale, Iaşi International Literature Festival
data.description: In Bucharest: Les Films de Cannes à Bucarest October 23 – November 1 This key event of the autumn film season, now at its 17th edition, hosts screenings at Elvire Popesco Cinema, Romanian Peasant Museum Cinema, the National Museum of Art of Romania, and Apolo 111. The festival is also held in Timișoara, Arad, Oradea, and Iași. More on the program here . Bucharest Scenography Biennale Until October 25 This international biennale of art and design is dedicated to scenography, performance design and stage technology. The 2026 edition is built around W.O.R.K. — Women. Oppression. Resistance. Knowledge. — the theme of its central exhibition, curated by Irina Moscu. More details here . National Theater Festival Until October 25 For ten days, the festival brings 36 productions in the official selection, with 88 performances in 24 halls, along with over 50 other events, hosted in 28 other cultural spaces in Bucharest. More details here . Art Safari Until December 20 The new season presents an exhibition about Brâncuși and the muses that influenced his creation, one about the Pop Art movement; photographs by Cristian Mungiu; as well as a series of other temporary exhibitions. More details here . BAD by Gregor Schneider October 24 – March 14, 2027 The exhibition by Gregor Schneider, one of Germany’s best-known contemporary artists, is open at the National Museum of Art of Romania (MNAR) and runs in parallel with the major exhibition “Gregor Schneider: Haus u r 2026” at Kunsthalle Düsseldorf. Wild Metaphysics Until October 24 The exhibition, open at Gaep, features six Brazilian artists whose works explore the extraordinary, the oneiric, and the metaphysical. The artists, whose work is presented in Romania for the first time, are Thiago Barbalho, Maria Nepomuceno, Mariana Rocha, Guga Szabzon, Marina Woisky, Michel Zózimo. More here . AccessABILITY Expo October 22 - October 23 The event, held at Politehnica University, gathers families, employers, public institutions, NGOs, healthcare providers, educators, and innovators "to turn accessibility from intent into implementation." More here . In the country: Picasso en visite Until January 17, 2027 The exhibition, presented by Art Encounters in Timișoara in partnership with Musée Picasso Antibes, brings together 69 works by Pablo Picasso, namely paintings, drawings, engravings, lithographs and ceramics, presented for the first time to the Romanian public. More here . BETA – Timișoara Architecture Biennial Until October 25 The event takes place under the theme “In Practice – as opposed to ‘in theory’” and will see more than 40 projects by participants from 15 countries transform the building of the former Ion Mincu High School. More here . Les Films de Cannes à Timişoara October 22 – October 25 Audiences are invited to Cinema Studio and Cinema Timiș to see the latest productions awarded at international festivals. More here . Astra Film Festival Until October 25 The festival, which takes place in Sibiu, runs a program of documentary films, conversations with filmmakers and guests, debates and meetings with audiences of all ages, as well as a special section dedicated to students. More details here . Iaşi International Festival of Literature and Translation October 21 - October 25 Paul Lynch, David Foenkinos, Parinoush Saniee and Aleksandar Hemon are among guests of this year’s literature festival in Iași. More on the program here .

data.title: USDA: Turkey turns to EU for sunflower imports, with Romania well placed to benefit
data.description: Romania and Bulgaria are well positioned to benefit, as both countries have recorded good harvests this year, Economica.net reported. Turkey has set a tariff quota of 1.25 million tonnes for the current marketing year, unchanged from previous years. However, it brought forward the introduction of reduced import duties on sunflower seeds, cutting the rate from 20% to 12% from October 1, rather than the usual November 30. The earlier start coincides with the peak harvest in the Black Sea region. “This is already having an impact on the markets in Romania and Bulgaria, with higher exports expected,” the USDA analysis noted. According to European Commission data, Romania has exported 160,121 tonnes of sunflower seeds outside the EU so far this marketing year, accounting for 79.2% of the bloc’s total exports. Bulgaria ranks second, with 25,286 tonnes. Turkey is the main destination, having purchased 158,801 tonnes of sunflower seeds from across the EU.

data.title: The Hidden Costs of "Doing It All" in HR
data.description: Year-end is when businesses decide what to keep investing in and what to rethink. For most HR departments that conversation starts from an uncomfortable position. The economy is stagnating, with 2026 growth forecasts between -0.5% and +0.1%. Leadership wants headcount and costs under control, yet expects HR to fill the roles the business cannot do without. Line managers still want a strong hire within weeks, even though specialist roles often take 4 to 6 weeks. Each vacancy draws around 60 applications, twice as many as in the previous year, so HR must screen far more people just to find the few who fit. At the same time, engineers, automation and quality specialists and mid-level managers remain hard to find. Business leaders also expect HR to absorb new obligations without extra resources: pay transparency rules, stricter limits on AI in hiring, and closer scrutiny of pay decisions. Add restructuring, with collective lay-offs up about 21% in 2025, and HR is often asked to manage departures quietly while keeping the remaining team motivated. The result is a function judged on speed, cost and quality all at once, with the same team that handled the work the year before. When one of the three slips, the business notices immediately. That is the hidden cost of "doing it all". Where the cost actually shows up Recruitment and search. The business sees an open position as lost output and an overloaded team. HR sees hundreds of CVs, a hiring manager who has changed the requirements twice, and a candidate who accepts another offer while the final interview is still being scheduled. For hard-to-fill roles, the search can mean starting over at new cost. Selection and assessment centres. When every vacancy attracts dozens of applicants, the temptation is to filter the CVs by an AI tool, or by instinct. The business then pays for this choice months later, through a bad hire, a restart, or a rejected candidate who challenges the process. Structured selection, including well-designed assessment centres, gives managers evidence they can rely upon and gives candidates a fair process. It also needs time and expertise that a stretched HR team rarely has. Performance evaluation. Pay rose about 3.5% this year against inflation of about 7%, so every feedback and pay conversation is harder than it was. At the same time, pay criteria must now be objective and neutral, and an unexplained gap above 5% triggers a joint assessment. Business leaders want evaluations that justify their pay decisions, while managers have little time to prepare them. A late or rushed evaluation costs trust now and weakens the evidence the company needs later. Outplacement. In 2025, in Romania, over 11,000 people lost their jobs in collective redundancies, and in January 2026 alone employers notified plans affecting more than 4,700 more. Severance covers the legal minimum. Support to find a new job is what the remaining employees notice, and what candidates will remember when the company needs to hire again. When the business asks for savings, outplacement is often the first item cut, even though it protects employer reputation in the long run. The team carrying it all. The following processes put the most strain on HR: recruitment, search & selection, assessment, performance evaluation and outplacement. These are intensive, sensitive tasks. They peak when a restructuring, a hiring wave or a new regulation arrives, and then they stop. A specialist consultancy brings what a single department rarely has: tested methods, experience from many similar situations, and capacity that scales with the workload. It also gives the business something hard to build internally, an objective, documented process that stands up to a candidate's challenge, a pay dispute or an audit. Your HR team stays focused on what only it can do, which is knowing the business, advising its leaders and looking after its people. The question is not whether to outsource, but which processes to hand over deliberately, before capacity runs out and the choice is made for you. A question worth asking before year-end: Which of these processes slows your HR down, and which would be best handled internally, standardised, passed to specialists or postponed? To help you decide, we developed a short survey (5 questions). Your answers to the Quick End of Year HR Services Survey will reveal, in a follow-up report, whether the bottlenecks you encounter are specific to you or common across Romanian employers.

data.title: Former Tazz, Profi executives launch Romanian local-producer marketplace Hambar
data.description: Alin Șerban, former CEO of Tazz, and Călin Costinaș, former deputy CEO of Profi, have launched Hambar, an online marketplace for Romanian local products. The platform aims to expand to more than 600 producers and 10,000 products within six months. Hambar’s initial catalog covers 10 categories, including pantry goods, dairy products, fish specialties, baked goods, meat, seasonal fruit and vegetables, and beverages. Customers can also order packages combining several items from the same producer. Before joining the platform, each producer is assessed by the Hambar team, including checks of the production site and manufacturing process, the company said. Producers receive individual profiles containing information about their businesses and the origin of their products. “Behind every good product is a producer who should be able to focus on what they do best, without having to become an expert in technology, marketing or logistics,” Alin Șerban, Hambar’s cofounder and CEO, said. “Our mission is to make it possible for an extraordinary product made in a Romanian village to reach customers throughout the country easily and safely.” Customers can purchase products from several producers in a single shopping cart, pay by card, and receive deliveries in Romania or other EU countries. Producers manage their products, inventory, and orders through a separate application. “Romania has an extraordinary world of small producers and people who are passionate about what they do, but too few of us know about them,” Călin Costinaș said. “With Hambar, we want to bring these two worlds closer together.” Hambar has also partnered with eMAG and Salt Bank. Users can log in with their eMAG accounts, while members of the Genius Moț program receive free delivery on two monthly orders worth at least RON 300, regardless of how many producers are included in the cart. Meanwhile, Salt Bank is the platform’s official banking partner. Hambar is available through customer and producer applications, as well as a desktop version.

data.translatedDescription: Alin Șerban, former CEO of Tazz, and Călin Costinaș, former deputy CEO of Profi, have launched Hambar, an online marketplace for Romanian local products. The platform aims to expand to more than 600 producers and 10,000 products within six months. Hambar’s initial catalog covers 10 categories, including pantry goods, dairy products, fish specialties, baked goods, meat, seasonal fruit and vegetables, and beverages. Customers can also order packages combining several items from the same producer. Before joining the platform, each producer is assessed by the Hambar team, including checks of the production site and manufacturing process, the company said. Producers receive individual profiles containing information about their businesses and the origin of their products. “Behind every good product is a producer who should be able to focus on what they do best, without having to become an expert in technology, marketing or logistics,” Alin Șerban, Hambar’s cofounder and CEO, said. “Our mission is to make it possible for an extraordinary product made in a Romanian village to reach customers throughout the country easily and safely.” Customers can purchase products from several producers in a single shopping cart, pay by card, and receive deliveries in Romania or other EU countries. Producers manage their products, inventory, and orders through a separate application. “Romania has an extraordinary world of small producers and people who are passionate about what they do, but too few of us know about them,” Călin Costinaș said. “With Hambar, we want to bring these two worlds closer together.” Hambar has also partnered with eMAG and Salt Bank. Users can log in with their eMAG accounts, while members of the Genius Moț program receive free delivery on two monthly orders worth at least RON 300, regardless of how many producers are included in the cart. Meanwhile, Salt Bank is the platform’s official banking partner. Hambar is available through customer and producer applications, as well as a desktop version.

data.title: Bucharest mayor remains under judicial supervision in bribery case
data.description: Bucharest mayor Ciprian Ciucu will remain under judicial supervision while prosecutors investigate him for alleged bribery. The Bucharest Tribunal on Wednesday, October 21, rejected his challenge against the National Anticorruption Directorate’s decision to extend the measure, Agerpres reported. The court also rejected Ciucu’s request to modify some of the obligations imposed on him. It ordered him to pay RON 500 in legal expenses, and the ruling is final. Ciprian Ciucu was placed under judicial supervision by the DNA in June . Prosecutors have since extended the measure twice, with the mayor unsuccessfully challenging each extension. “I presented my case, and I hoped that this time the judicial supervision would be lifted,” the mayor said after leaving the court. “I will challenge it every time because I consider myself innocent.” He also said he wanted to complete his term without the restrictions and denied that he posed a flight risk. Prosecutors allege that during the November-December 2025 election campaign, Ciprian Ciucu received advertising and campaign consulting services from two businesspeople in exchange for issuing a permit and an urban-planning certificate for a real estate project. At the time of the alleged acts in November 2025, Ciucu was serving as mayor of District 6.

data.title: Călin Georgescu questioned over alleged search for surveillance devices in his villa near Bucharest
data.description: Former presidential candidate Călin Georgescu was questioned by DIICOT prosecutors on Wednesday, October 21, in a case in which he is suspected of having asked a man to scan his villa in Mogoșoaia, near Bucharest, to find out whether investigators had installed recording devices in the house. The man who allegedly searched the villa for equipment installed by prosecutors is also being questioned by DIICOT. “The criminal investigation revealed that on September 26, 2026, a 35-year-old suspect, at the request of another suspect, aged 64 (who is a defendant in another case handled by the DIICOT Central Office), proceeded to scan/check the latter’s property in the commune of Mogoșoaia, Ilfov County, intending to identify audio-video recording equipment used by judicial authorities, as well as altering computer data or disrupting the functioning of computer systems used to implement technical surveillance measures,” DIICOT announced in a press release. Judicial sources told Agerpres that the 64-year-old man is Călin Georgescu. According to DIICOT, the sweep took place after prosecutors carried out a home search at the property in question as part of a criminal case in which technical surveillance measures had also been implemented, circumstances known to the two suspects. “The intended outcome, namely the alteration of computer data and the disruption or damage of the technical equipment used by judicial authorities, did not occur for reasons beyond the suspects’ control. The questioning is taking place at the DIICOT Central Office,” prosecutors announced. On September 21, Călin Georgescu was stopped in traffic and taken home, where investigators searched his residence. After seven hours of searches, masked officers emerged from the villa carrying bags full of documents. On the same day, investigators found a signal jammer in Călin Georgescu’s car, which allowed the former presidential candidate to avoid being recorded while having various conversations. The Bucharest Tribunal approved on Tuesday, October 13, the request submitted by former presidential candidate Cǎlin Georgescu to replace pretrial detention with 30 days of house arrest. The ruling is not final and will take effect only if upheld following the appeal period.

data.title: SAP Romania expands Timișoara office amid growth of local team
data.description: SAP Romania, the local subsidiary of the global leader in enterprise applications and Business AI, announced the opening of a new office space in Timișoara on Wednesday, October 21, following the growth of its local team and the high occupancy rate of its existing headquarters. “Timișoara is an important center for SAP’s operations in Romania, with a team that has grown steadily in recent years, and the office expansion is a natural response to this development. We want to provide our colleagues with a working environment adapted to their needs, which facilitates collaboration and the exchange of ideas,” said Diana David, Managing Director of SAP Romania. The expansion was carried out by fitting out an additional floor in the same campus where the company already operates, and the decision came in response to the increase in the number of employees in recent years, which has led to more intensive use of the existing space. As the available workspaces no longer met the team’s needs, the project aimed to adapt the office’s capacity to its current size, as well as improve conditions for individual work and collaboration among colleagues. “The SAP office in Timișoara hosts teams specializing in Business AI platforms, industry-specific product development, Cloud Operations and consulting services, as well as industry-specific SAP solutions, such as those for the automotive industry. These teams contribute to the adoption of SAP’s most innovative solutions in this era of digital transformation driven by AI,” added Dan Beșleagă, a member of SAP Romania’s management team and Head of Business Technology Platform Global Delivery Hub at SAP Romania. With the addition of the new space, covering 1,530 square meters, SAP’s office in Timișoara now has a total area of 3,474 square meters and a capacity of 282 workspaces, up from 162 previously. The expansion allows employees to be distributed more efficiently throughout the available space and addresses the high occupancy rate recorded before the project began, according to the company. In addition to the 120 extra workstations, the new floor includes 14 meeting rooms of various sizes, a room dedicated to design thinking sessions, a Work Café, and relaxation areas, including a space for children. The project was initiated in January 2026, and the fit-out works took place between April and July this year. The new space became operational on August 3, when employees began using it, while the official inauguration took place on October 20, 2026. With a presence in Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca, and Timișoara, SAP Romania has more than 1,200 employees and hosts one of the company’s strongest Service Delivery teams in Eastern Europe. The expertise developed locally supports SAP projects and operations internationally, with the specialized skills of teams in Romania being leveraged by colleagues around the world. In the local market, SAP works with more than 700 active clients, supporting the digitalization of organizations of various sizes, including small and medium-sized enterprises, which account for the majority of active companies in Romania.

data.title: Colliers: Romania reaches 5 million sqm of retail space, room to grow in smaller cities
data.description: Real estate consultancy Colliers took stock of Romania’s development in terms of retail space in an in-depth analysis marking 30 years of activity in the country, highlighting that room to grow still exists in small and medium-sized cities. “In 1996, when Colliers entered the Romanian market, modern retail was only just emerging. That same year, Metro opened the country’s first cash-and-carry store, at a time when most shopping still took place in markets, department stores and traditional retail formats,” Colliers said in a press release. Bucharest Mall (1999) and the first Carrefour hypermarket (2001) followed, and within just a few years, modern retail began expanding rapidly from Bucharest into Romania’s major cities, supported by rising incomes, broader access to credit and the country’s approaching accession to the European Union. “In the early 2000s, Romania’s modern retail stock was estimated at only around 100,000 square meters, compared with more than 5 million square meters today. The difference illustrates just how much both the real estate market and the way Romanians shop and consume have changed within a single generation,” the report mentioned. Romania’s accession to the European Union gave the market a major boost, as real incomes were rising, access to credit was expanding, and international retailers viewed Romania as one of the markets with the strongest growth potential in the region. The market did not, however, grow at a constant pace. The boom ahead of the global financial crisis brought some of Romania’s largest retail developments, with around 400,000 - 500,000 square meters of new retail space delivered each year in 2007-2008. The crisis brought that pace of development to an abrupt halt, with many projects postponed, frozen or abandoned. AFI Cotroceni, covering approximately 76,000 square meters, opened in 2009, at the height of the recession, and later became one of the strongest-performing shopping centers in the market. The 2009-2013 period also highlighted the importance of a shopping center’s position within a city. Strong projects continued to attract tenants even during difficult years, while others lost ground or exited the market. Following the crisis, developers became more cautious, placing greater emphasis on location, purchasing power and the real potential of each catchment area. Another major shift came with the expansion of retail parks, which brought modern retail to towns with populations of below 50,000 inhabitants. Lower development costs compared with traditional shopping centers made such projects viable in locations that previously had very few modern shopping options. Retail parks have significantly reshaped Romania’s modern retail landscape precisely because they can operate successfully in smaller towns where a more expensive shopping center development would not be successful. While the 2000s were dominated by large shopping centers and landmark projects, recent years have brought greater geographical expansion and formats better suited to smaller cities. This shift is also reflected in recent deliveries. Romania passed the 5 million square meter threshold of modern retail space in 2025, when approximately 185,000 square meters were delivered across 13 projects, following a 2020-2024 period in which annual deliveries averaged around 145,000 square meters. For 2026, Colliers estimates approximately 150,000 square meters of new retail space, slightly below last year’s level, with a solid pipeline for 2027. ”Romanian retail has expanded considerably, but in recent years, consumers have moved even faster. Purchasing power in Romania is now much closer to levels seen in Central European markets, yet the country still has a much lower density of modern retail space. The gap is particularly visible in small and medium-sized cities, where we continue to see interest from both developers and retailers and where there is still room for new projects,” explained Liana Dumitru, Director, Retail Agency at Colliers. Romania has around 270 square meters of modern retail space per 1,000 inhabitants, compared with approximately 400-500 in Hungary, Czechia and Poland. The gap is particularly significant given how much Romanians’ purchasing power has increased over the past three decades. Colliers also noted that while at a national level, the gap between Romania has a retail stock around 1.7x smaller than in Czechia and Poland on a per capita basis, the gap grows to 2.7x in case of cities with a population of below 100,000 inhabitants. Although consumption growth slowed in 2025-2026, Colliers consultants see this period as one of consolidation following several years of strong expansion, rather than a change in direction. Developer interest in new retail development sites returned towards the end of 2025, indicating that new projects are already being prepared for the period through to 2030. The market’s growing maturity is also reflected in major investment transactions. In 2026, AFI Europe acquired six MAS retail assets for a gross transaction value of around EUR 297 million, in the largest retail transaction in the history of the local market. Two decades earlier, the sale of Polus Center Cluj for more than EUR 200 million marked the point at which retail began to be viewed as an important institutional real estate investment.

data.title: Romanian seventh-grader who attacked teacher, fellow student with knife “appears to show no remorse”
data.description: The chief prosecutor of the Bistrița-Năsăud Tribunal, Adrian Briciu, said on Tuesday, October 21, that the seventh-grade student who attacked a teacher and several children at a school in Bistrița with a knife had “extremist, Legionary-extremist, far-right symbols” on him and that he premeditated the attack. The student came to school that day with a military-style helmet, a balaclava, gloves, and a pocketknife, according to the prosecutor. He got dressed in the bathroom, where investigators found messages in English and “extremist, Legionary-extremist, far-right symbols.” Prosecutors found that the student did not regret his actions and did not appear to feel remorse. “On October 19, 2026, at around 8:00–8:30 AM, a 13-year-old minor, a seventh-grade student at a lower secondary school in the city of Bistrița, went to school carrying, more specifically in his school backpack, a military-style helmet, a balaclava and gloves, as well as a pocketknife. He went there with the intention of physically assaulting a sixth-grade student who attended the same school as the attacker, motivated by the fact that he considered him Indian, most likely due to his darker skin color,” Bistrița-Năsăud Tribunal chief prosecutor Adrian Briciu said, cited by News.ro . According to him, the student entered the bathroom, where he got dressed, and then went to the door of the classroom attended by the targeted student. He was met by the teacher, whom he attacked and struck several times. The assault stopped only when another student rushed to help. Adrian Briciu said the act had been premeditated, “given that he had prepared at home with that mask, gloves, and helmet.” He explained that the attacker “was not perceived as a person who felt remorse.” “He did not behave in a way that suggested he regretted his actions. He did not seem like a person who was affected; I do not know to what extent he is aware of what he has done,” Adrian Briciu further stated. He reiterated that the adolescent is not criminally liable. “From a criminal law perspective, no measures can be taken because he is not criminally liable, and the measures that can be taken fall outside our jurisdiction, so to speak. They can be taken by the Directorate General for Social Assistance and Child Protection, in the form of specialized supervision measures,” the cited source further stated. The student has not yet been questioned, nor have his parents. His father is abroad, while his mother is with him at the hospital in Cluj. Meanwhile, the 28-year-old teacher who was attacked is recovering well and is still hospitalized, according to the authorities. Newly-confirmed Romanian prime minister Luca Niculescu commented on the attack on Wednesday, October 21, noting that a “concrete action plan” should be drawn up “as quickly as possible,” involving several institutions. Niculescu said that the first topic he discussed with the ministers of the new government was school safety, particularly after the attack at a school in Bistrița. The prime minister also expressed “full solidarity and compassion with the teacher and the student who were injured.” “I want to make it very clear that there are no excuses for violence, and I have decided, together with these ministers, to draw up a concrete action plan as quickly as possible, involving several institutions, including the Ministry of Internal Affairs, alongside specialists, teachers, student associations, and psychologists, to come up with quick solutions. We need to address several aspects, but this is one of the essential priorities for the education ministers,” Luca Niculescu also said, cited by News.ro .

data.title: Board of Directors of Romania’s central bank ups inflation forecast for 2026
data.description: The annual inflation rate will increase by the end of 2026 and exceed the 6.1% previously forecast by the National Bank of Romania, according to the minutes of the monetary policy meeting on October 8, published on Tuesday, October 20. Members of the BNR Board of Directors said the new economic data indicate a deterioration in the short-term inflation outlook compared with the estimates presented in August. The previous forecast anticipated an annual rate of 6.1% in December 2026, followed by a gradual decline to 2.8% in June 2028. New factors, particularly the rising fuel and energy prices, higher raw material prices, and movements in the leu exchange rate, may lead to increased inflation. “Board members noted that, according to the new data and analyses, the annual inflation rate will follow an upward trajectory until the end of the current year, thus exceeding the figures in the medium-term forecast from August 2026, which anticipated it reaching 6.1% in December 2026 and subsequently declining to 2.8% in June 2028,” the document stated, cited by Digi24 . The central bank warned that a prolonged conflict in the Middle East could intensify inflationary pressures, including through higher prices for imported goods. Developments in international oil and raw material markets therefore continue to represent a significant source of uncertainty for Romania’s economy. “At the same time, it was agreed that the balance of risks induced by supply-side factors remains tilted upward in the short term, particularly given the uncertainties surrounding the prices of crude oil and other raw materials in the context of the prolonged conflict in the Middle East, as well as their potential direct and indirect effects domestically, including through the prices of certain imported intermediate and finished goods,” according to the document. However, there are also factors that could limit price increases. Board members highlighted the favorable results recorded this year in certain crop production sectors, with positive effects on the prices of vegetables, fruit, and eggs, as well as other agri-food products. At the same time, developments in household consumption and economic demand could moderate the pass-through of higher energy and fuel costs to the prices of goods and services. In its analysis of recent developments, the BNR highlighted the significant decline in the annual inflation rate during the first two months of the third quarter, from 10.42% in June to 6.17% in August 2026, as the direct effects of the removal of the electricity price cap and the increases in VAT rates and excise duties introduced the previous year faded. At the same time, the annual CORE2 adjusted inflation rate, an indicator that excludes a range of volatile and administered prices from the calculation, fell from 8.3% in June to 6.2% in August. This development was driven by slower increases in processed food prices and a moderation in price rises for non-food goods and services. At its meeting on October 8, 2026, the BNR Board of Directors unanimously decided to keep the monetary policy rate at 6.50% per year. The interest rate on the lending facility (Lombard) was also maintained at 7.50% per year, while the rate on the deposit facility remained at 5.50% per year. In a separate analysis presented the same day at a conference organized by Coface Romania, analysts said that Romania’s economic growth in 2027 could be between 0.5% and 2%. “The overall picture is one of moderate optimism, also taking into account the economic growth outlooks recently provided by both the International Monetary Fund and the European Commission, and the message from discussions with investment firms is that, more likely, we will have economic growth of around 2% next year. This is somewhat close to the economic growth outlooks for Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic as well. Therefore, we are broadly following the regional trend,” said Florian Neagu, director within the Financial Stability Department of the National Bank of Romania (BNR), cited by Economedia .
data.translatedTitle: Board of Directors of Romania’s central bank ups inflation forecast for 2026
data.translatedDescription: The annual inflation rate will increase by the end of 2026 and exceed the 6.1% previously forecast by the National Bank of Romania, according to the minutes of the monetary policy meeting on October 8, published on Tuesday, October 20. Members of the BNR Board of Directors said the new economic data indicate a deterioration in the short-term inflation outlook compared with the estimates presented in August. The previous forecast anticipated an annual rate of 6.1% in December 2026, followed by a gradual decline to 2.8% in June 2028. New factors, particularly the rising fuel and energy prices, higher raw material prices, and movements in the leu exchange rate, may lead to increased inflation. “Board members noted that, according to the new data and analyses, the annual inflation rate will follow an upward trajectory until the end of the current year, thus exceeding the figures in the medium-term forecast from August 2026, which anticipated it reaching 6.1% in December 2026 and subsequently declining to 2.8% in June 2028,” the document stated, cited by Digi24 . The central bank warned that a prolonged conflict in the Middle East could intensify inflationary pressures, including through higher prices for imported goods. Developments in international oil and raw material markets therefore continue to represent a significant source of uncertainty for Romania’s economy. “At the same time, it was agreed that the balance of risks induced by supply-side factors remains tilted upward in the short term, particularly given the uncertainties surrounding the prices of crude oil and other raw materials in the context of the prolonged conflict in the Middle East, as well as their potential direct and indirect effects domestically, including through the prices of certain imported intermediate and finished goods,” according to the document. However, there are also factors that could limit price increases. Board members highlighted the favorable results recorded this year in certain crop production sectors, with positive effects on the prices of vegetables, fruit, and eggs, as well as other agri-food products. At the same time, developments in household consumption and economic demand could moderate the pass-through of higher energy and fuel costs to the prices of goods and services. In its analysis of recent developments, the BNR highlighted the significant decline in the annual inflation rate during the first two months of the third quarter, from 10.42% in June to 6.17% in August 2026, as the direct effects of the removal of the electricity price cap and the increases in VAT rates and excise duties introduced the previous year faded. At the same time, the annual CORE2 adjusted inflation rate, an indicator that excludes a range of volatile and administered prices from the calculation, fell from 8.3% in June to 6.2% in August. This development was driven by slower increases in processed food prices and a moderation in price rises for non-food goods and services. At its meeting on October 8, 2026, the BNR Board of Directors unanimously decided to keep the monetary policy rate at 6.50% per year. The interest rate on the lending facility (Lombard) was also maintained at 7.50% per year, while the rate on the deposit facility remained at 5.50% per year. This is somewhat close to the economic growth outlooks for Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic as well. Therefore, we are broadly following the regional trend,” said Florian Neagu, director within the Financial Stability Department of the National Bank of Romania (BNR), cited by Economedia .

data.title: Report: Bucharest flexible office market grows sixfold since 2015
data.description: Bucharest has at least 46 flexible office centers operated by 24 companies, according to a Cushman & Wakefield Echinox report. Their combined area has grown from 11,100 square meters in 2015 to roughly 73,500 sqm in 2026. Flexible space represents around 2.1% of Bucharest’s total office stock. This compares with 4% in Warsaw, 3.9% in Prague and Sofia, and 2.3% in Bratislava. Warsaw has the region’s largest flex office market by volume, at approximately 250,000 sqm, followed by Prague with 153,300 sqm, and Sofia with 92,000 sqm. Bucharest ranks fourth, ahead of Bratislava, which has 40,500 square meters. “The growth of this segment reflects a broader shift in the way companies plan their workplace strategies,” said Mădălina Cojocaru, partner in the Office Agency division at Cushman & Wakefield Echinox. “For occupiers, flexible workspace is no longer seen merely as a solution to temporary needs, but increasingly as a complementary piece of their overall office approach.” Companies use such spaces for project teams, satellite offices, and adjustments to changing staff levels, she explained. Central-western Bucharest hosts the largest volume, with eight centers totaling 16,000 sqm, or 21.8% of the city’s flex office stock. The central area has the highest proportion of flexible offices within its local office inventory, at 3.2%, spread across 12 locations totaling 14,500 sqm. Meanwhile, Floreasca-Barbu Văcărescu has 10,400 sqm across seven locations, followed by the central business district with 10,300 sqm, and Dimitrie Pompeiu with 9,700 sqm. At the opposite end, Eastern Bucharest has no coworking center. Local companies represent 62% of operators, while international providers account for 38%. The four largest players - IWG through Regus and Spaces, aSpace, HOTSPOT, and Mindspace - control 63% of the available stock. Monthly rates generally range from EUR 150 to EUR 450 per desk, excluding VAT. Private offices cost approximately EUR 300 to EUR 500 per person per month, depending on the location, workspace, and services included, the same report said.

data.title: Diana Nicolaie named CEO of Romania’s Art Safari New Museum
data.description: Diana Nicolaie took over as CEO of Art Safari New Museum on October 20, the Bucharest cultural institution announced. She succeeds Ioana Ciocan, who had led Art Safari since 2015. During Ciocan’s tenure, Art Safari developed into a national cultural project, organizing 19 editions and attracting more than 1 million visitors. Diana Nicolaie has already worked extensively with the organization. She designed the architectural concept for its new venue at 13 Amzei Square in Bucharest and coordinated several exhibitions. Her projects include Bags: Inside Out , organized in partnership with London’s Victoria and Albert Museum; Enescu and the Minotaur , developed with the George Enescu International Festival; Romanian History in 100 Portraits ; and R: Eminescu. The Rational Poet . She has also coordinated exhibitions in the museum’s current season, including War and Peace , Pop Art. A World in Color , and Cristian Mungiu. Fjord, Photographs . “I am honored to receive the baton from Ioana Ciocan and lead Art Safari New Museum, a landmark on Romania’s artistic and cultural scene,” Diana Nicolaie stated. “I fully feel both the joy and the responsibility of continuing the team’s work over the past 12 years.” She also said the institution would continue developing exhibitions based on audience interests, forming partnerships with Romanian and international museums and artists, and making art accessible to younger generations. A graduate of the Ion Mincu University of Architecture and Urban Planning and the Bucharest University of Economic Studies, Nicolaie has nearly two decades of experience in design. She expanded her practice into visual art in 2023, presenting exhibitions in Bucharest and New York.

data.title: Seven in ten Romanians plan Black Friday purchases in 2026, study finds
data.description: Seven in ten Romanians ages 18 to 55 plan to shop during Black Friday 2026, according to an MKOR survey. The 70% purchase-intent rate compares with 62% in 2025 and 57% in both 2023 and 2024. The interest is similar among men and women, at 71% and 70%, respectively, although their planned purchases differ. Still, electronics and appliances rank first for both groups, cited by 55% of women and 47% of men who intend to shop. IT and communications products, including phones, laptops, and smartwatches, are sought by 44% of male shoppers, compared with 29% of women. Men also report greater interest in gaming products and automotive items. Among women planning purchases, 37% intend to buy cosmetics, perfumes, or personal care products, compared with 17% of men. Clothing, footwear, and accessories are also on the lists of 37% of women and 24% of men. Six in ten prospective buyers plan to shop exclusively online, up from 47% in 2025, the same survey found. Only 8% expect to buy solely from physical stores, compared with 12% last year. The average planned budget is approximately RON 2,100, close to the RON 2,046 reported in 2025. Around 86% of prospective shoppers have set their budget in advance. NETOPIA Payments data showed that the value of payments processed on Black Friday 2025 increased by 19% from the previous year. The average card payment reached RON 400, around 60% above the annual daily average. The MKOR survey was conducted online between September 18 and 23 among 1,000 Romanian residents ages 18 to 55. It has a stated margin of error of ±3.1% at a 95% confidence level.

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. data.title: APANHA-SE MAIS DEPRESSA UM MENTIROSO QUE UM COXO!
data.description:
DSP através da sua equipa de "Lambe-Botas" está cavando cada vez mais a sua própria cova, adiantando cada vez mais o seu fim. Somente alguns acreditavam que foi ele quem estava por trás do "Progresso Nacional" o blog onde começou toda essa história de Mentiras, Calunias, Difamações, Ameaças e tantos outros agressões tóxicas ao espírito humano, a todos os que não estão do seu lado e cujo o único objectivo, era ser chamado de rei dos réis da Guiné. Comandou o Progresso Nacional assim como Bin Laden comandou a Al-Qaeda e acabou por fracassar. Pensou, repensou e resolveu voltar novamente ainda com mais TERROR e está a comandar o Guiné Puro tentando levar toda a nação ao abismo assim como o ISIS quer levar a humanidade. Camaradas, Guiné Puro assim como o falecido Progresso Nacional é o reflexo do espirito de DSP, alí é possivel ver tudo e quanto o sujeito é baixo. DSP é um hipócrita e um anarquista moderno. "ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E COMPRAS?!" essa foi uma das frases da recente publicação que mostram por quem e para que fim, é dirigido o Guiné Puro ou melhor o blog do terror como podem ver já a seguir. Demonstraram mais uma vez claramente que o "MCCI" pertence a DPS, pois uma publicação dessa no próprio blog do ganancioso só pode ser das duas uma: "Boca capli elis ou Foronta passanta e dicidi ca sucundi rostu". Camaradas, Domingos Simões Pereira afundou seu próprio barco devido a sua ganância e complexo de superioridade. "I pirigu pa i faladu ba cuma, el i unicu alguim cu bai escola na Guiné" seu ultimo desejo é "afundar com todos, inclusive o PAIGC". __________PARA A VOSSA CONFIRMAÇÃO, AQUI ESTÁ A PUBLICAÇÃO_________ MARCOS GALINA BARBOSA VAI PERCEBER QUE METEU COM GENTE

TEMOS ALGUÉM NO AEROPORTO PARA NOS INFOMAR O DIA EM QUE EL CHEGAR. INVENTOU

data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: Eerste olieboringen GranMorgu starten in december, project al voor 43 procent gerealiseerd
data.description: Suriname staat voor een belangrijke stap in de ontwikkeling van zijn offshore olie-industrie. In december beginnen de eerste productieboringen voor het GranMorgu-project, dat inmiddels voor 43 procent is gerealiseerd. Minister Patrick Brunings meldt dat de voorbereidingen volgens schema verlopen en dat de boorschepen binnenkort worden verwacht.
